scenario: A security group permits TCP 8883 (MQTT/TLS) inbound from 0.0.0.0/0 on the connected vehicle telemetry ingestion fleet. The scanner flags it as a broadly open port. However, the MQTT broker requires mTLS client certificates issued by Hyundai's internal vehicle PKI, and unauthenticated connections are rejected at the TLS handshake layer before any data is processed.
why_misclassified: Scanner evaluates network-layer reachability only; it cannot inspect TLS mutual authentication requirements at the application layer. EC-08: traffic is VPC-bounded from the scanner's perspective but the legitimate internet-facing MQTT port appears as 'open'.
detection_signal: SecurityGroup sg-0a1b2c3d allows inbound TCP 8883 from 0.0.0.0/0 — HIGH: unrestricted inbound on non-standard port
ground_truth: Port 8883 requires valid vehicle-issued mTLS client certs. No unauthenticated session can establish. This is intentional V2C architecture per UNECE WP.29 Annex 5 requirements.
remediation_impact: Restricting to a static CIDR would break OTA telemetry from millions of vehicles with dynamic IP addresses globally. MQTT clients connect from mobile networks with carrier NAT.

scenario: S3 bucket adas-map-tiles-prod is configured with public read access. CSPM tool reports CRITICAL data exposure. The bucket exclusively contains pre-rendered HD map tiles used by ADAS navigation — the same data served by commercial map providers. No PII, vehicle telemetry, or proprietary data is stored here; it is intentionally public CDN-origin content.
why_misclassified: EC-52: automotive sub-system severity multiplier incorrectly applied. Scanner sees 'ADAS' in bucket tag and inflates severity assuming safety-critical data. The data sensitivity classifier cannot distinguish map imagery from sensor fusion logs.
detection_signal: S3 bucket adas-map-tiles-prod has public ACL — CRITICAL: automotive safety-critical data potentially exposed
ground_truth: Bucket contains only publicly licensed HD map tiles (cartographic data). Data is intentionally distributed publicly to vehicle head units. No vehicle-identifying or safety-critical sensor data present.
remediation_impact: Making the bucket private would break HD map delivery to ADAS subsystems in all production vehicles, degrading navigation and potentially triggering fail-safe ADAS degradation modes.

scenario: IAM role arn:aws:iam::HAEA-KIA-PROD:role/shared-telematics-reader has a trust policy permitting assume-role from the HYUNDAI-HAEA-PROD account. CSPM flags this as unauthorized cross-account access. In reality, this is the documented HAEA shared services architecture where Hyundai and Kia telematics data pipelines share a common ingestion layer under a formal intra-org data sharing agreement.
why_misclassified: EC-27: intra-org trust is treated as external account access. Scanner does not resolve AWS Organizations membership to differentiate partner-org accounts from truly external principals.
detection_signal: IAM role allows cross-account access from account 123456789012 — HIGH: potential privilege escalation from external account
ground_truth: Both accounts are members of the HAEA AWS Organization. The trust relationship is documented in the HAEA Cross-Brand Data Governance policy and reviewed quarterly under TISAX AL2 requirements.
remediation_impact: Removing the trust policy breaks the Hyundai-Kia shared telematics ingestion pipeline, which processes ~2M vehicle events/hour and feeds fleet management dashboards.

scenario: OTA update distribution servers have security group rules permitting inbound HTTPS (443) from 0.0.0.0/0. CSPM marks this CRITICAL as internet-exposed fleet management infrastructure. The OTA endpoint is behind AWS WAF with geo-restrictions, rate limiting, and requires firmware signature verification. The broad SG rule exists because vehicle IP addresses are globally distributed across all mobile carriers.
why_misclassified: EC-17: NACL and WAF compensating controls are not evaluated. Scanner sees the SG in isolation without correlating WAF WebACL associations or Network ACL deny rules for non-HTTPS ports.
detection_signal: SecurityGroup sg-ota-prod allows inbound TCP 443 from 0.0.0.0/0 — CRITICAL: fleet management infrastructure internet-exposed
ground_truth: OTA endpoint is intentionally internet-accessible per UNECE WP.29 cybersecurity requirements for remote vehicle software updates. WAF enforces strict request validation and firmware packages require RSA-4096 signature verification.
remediation_impact: Restricting to a CIDR range is technically impossible — vehicles connect from mobile IPs across 40+ countries. Lockdown would halt safety-critical firmware distribution.

scenario: Azure App Service hosting a V2X simulation environment has anonymous access enabled for a REST API endpoint. CSPM reports HIGH risk identity exposure. This is a non-networked development environment used by ADAS engineers to simulate vehicle-to-infrastructure communication using synthetic data. The app service is not peered to any production network and contains no real vehicle data.
why_misclassified: EC-09: dev environment inflation. The scanner applies prod-level severity thresholds without considering the environment tag. The App Service is tagged env=dev-simulation but the tag is not evaluated in the severity scoring logic.
detection_signal: App Service adas-v2x-sim-dev has anonymous authentication — HIGH: unauthenticated access to automotive infrastructure
ground_truth: This is an isolated dev simulation environment with synthetic V2X payloads. No production data, no network path to production systems. Engineers need frictionless access to run simulation loops.
remediation_impact: Requiring auth in this environment would add 30+ minutes of setup friction per simulation session for 15 ADAS engineers, significantly slowing ISO 21434 compliance testing cycles.

scenario: RDS instance vehicle-telemetry-archive has publicly_accessible=true flagged by CSPM as HIGH risk data exposure. The database stores aggregated vehicle diagnostic codes for warranty analysis. The instance is deployed in private subnets with no internet gateway route, and the security group only permits port 5432 from the application VPC CIDR. The publicly_accessible attribute was set by a Terraform module default and never corrected.
why_misclassified: EC-37: RDS publicly_accessible flag in private subnet. The scanner checks the API attribute value without verifying the actual network path. Route table analysis would show no internet-reachable path exists.
detection_signal: RDS instance vehicle-telemetry-archive has publicly_accessible=true — HIGH: production vehicle database exposed to internet
ground_truth: Instance is in a private subnet with no IGW or NAT route to the internet. The publicly_accessible=true flag is a Terraform module artifact. Network-layer analysis confirms the database is not reachable from outside the VPC.
remediation_impact: While setting publicly_accessible=false is correct hygiene, the urgency is low — no actual exposure exists. Automated remediation without testing could trigger a brief DB endpoint change causing application connectivity errors.

scenario: ECR container image for the ADAS data pipeline is flagged for CVE-2024-21626 (runc container escape, CVSS 8.6). The container runs on Amazon Linux 2023 on EKS. The CVE affects runc versions on systems using certain Linux kernel configurations. However, the EKS node AMI uses a patched runc version (1.1.12+), and the CVE was patched in the AMI months before this scan.
why_misclassified: EC-34: cross-platform or version-specific CVE mismatch. Scanner detects the CVE reference in a base image layer but does not cross-reference the actual installed runc binary version on the node or verify the Amazon Linux patch status.
detection_signal: ECR image adas-pipeline:v2.4.1 — CRITICAL: CVE-2024-21626 runc container escape vulnerability in automotive safety pipeline
ground_truth: EKS node group uses AMI ami-0abc123 (Amazon Linux 2023, runc 1.1.12) which includes the runc patch. The image-level CVE reference is a metadata artifact; the runtime component is patched.
remediation_impact: Forcing image rebuild for an already-patched CVE wastes 2-3 hours of pipeline time and may introduce regression risk from unnecessary dependency updates.

scenario: Azure Key Vault key vehicle-data-cmk shows expiry date of 30 days. CSPM reports HIGH severity for impending key expiration in a TISAX-certified environment. The key is managed under an automated rotation policy that rotates the key 7 days before expiry and the expiry date is automatically extended. This key rotation has run successfully for 18 consecutive months.
why_misclassified: EC-25: immutable rotation schedule misread as impending failure. The scanner detects the key's current expiry window but does not evaluate whether an automated rotation policy exists or whether the rotation has a successful execution history.
detection_signal: Key Vault key vehicle-data-cmk expires in 30 days — HIGH: TISAX-scope encryption key approaching expiry without confirmed rotation
ground_truth: Key rotation policy is configured and has successfully auto-rotated 18 times. The expiry date observed is the post-rotation target window, not a lapsed key. Zero manual intervention required.
remediation_impact: Manual key rotation initiated by security team would interfere with the automated policy, potentially creating a double-rotation event and requiring key version updates across dependent services.

scenario: CSPM reports CloudTrail is not enabled in the HAEA-KIA-Sandbox account. The account is used for vehicle simulation testing only. However, the HAEA AWS Organization has an organization-level CloudTrail configured in the management account that covers all member accounts including sandbox accounts, with S3 logs centralized in the security account.
why_misclassified: EC-19: org-level logging compensating control. The scanner checks for a CloudTrail trail within the account boundary but does not detect organization-level trails applied from the management account.
detection_signal: Account HAEA-KIA-Sandbox has no CloudTrail trail enabled — HIGH: ISO 21434 audit logging requirement not met
ground_truth: Organization CloudTrail arn:aws:cloudtrail:us-east-1:MGMT-ACCOUNT:trail/haea-org-trail covers all accounts in the AWS Organization including sandbox accounts. All API calls are logged to centralized S3.
remediation_impact: Creating a redundant account-level trail would double logging costs (~$800/month per active account) and create duplicate events in the SIEM, increasing alert noise.

scenario: Lambda function vin-decoder-prod has a Node.js dependency flagged for CVE-2024-37890 in ws (WebSocket library, CVSS 7.5). The vulnerability requires an attacker to send a specially crafted WebSocket frame. However, this Lambda function is a VIN decoding service that only processes HTTP REST calls — it has no WebSocket server, and the ws package is a transitive devDependency of a testing framework, never loaded at runtime.
why_misclassified: EC-43: build-time dependency flagged as runtime. The scanner parses package-lock.json which includes devDependencies bundled during the CI artifact build. The ws package is only present in the test harness, not in the Lambda handler execution path.
detection_signal: Lambda vin-decoder-prod contains CVE-2024-37890 (ws WebSocket DoS) — HIGH: connected vehicle identifier service vulnerable to denial of service
ground_truth: ws is a devDependency of jest-environment-jsdom, used only in the CI test suite. The Lambda deployment package contains only production dependencies; ws is excluded from the bundle via webpack externals config.
remediation_impact: Forcing upgrade of a test-only transitive dependency requires regression testing of the full test suite with no security benefit to the production Lambda.

scenario: GCP firewall rule v2x-rsu-ingest-allow permits UDP 5900-5910 from 0.0.0.0/0, used for V2X RSU (Road Side Unit) telemetry ingestion. CSPM flags this as a broad open rule. The receiving Cloud Run instances are within a VPC Service Perimeter that restricts data egress, and the UDP range is only accepted from a Cloud Armor security policy restricting source IPs to registered RSU hardware subnets.
why_misclassified: EC-06: CIDR-gated at a layer above the firewall. The scanner evaluates firewall rules in isolation without correlating the Cloud Armor backend security policy that provides the actual source IP restriction.
detection_signal: Firewall rule v2x-rsu-ingest-allow allows UDP 5900-5910 from 0.0.0.0/0 — HIGH: V2X infrastructure exposed to arbitrary internet sources
ground_truth: Cloud Armor security policy restricts inbound traffic to 47 registered RSU hardware subnet CIDRs. The 0.0.0.0/0 firewall rule is a technical requirement because Cloud Armor operates as an intermediary — actual ingress is gated.
remediation_impact: Modifying the firewall rule to specific CIDRs would conflict with Cloud Armor's operation model and requires infrastructure redesign. The current two-layer approach is the GCP-recommended pattern for UDP workloads.

scenario: Azure Defender for Cloud reports a CRITICAL vulnerability on the vehicle data lake processing VM. The underlying CVE has a CVSS score of 9.1. However, Defender for Cloud maps Microsoft's own severity scale (Critical = CVSS 9+) to the CSPM aggregator's scale which uses Critical for CVSS 9.5+. The actual CVSS score of 9.1 should map to HIGH in the aggregator's normalized scale.
why_misclassified: EC-47: CSP severity scale non-equivalence. Microsoft Defender uses a 4-tier scale (Critical/High/Medium/Low) mapped differently than AWS Inspector or GCP SCC. The aggregator ingests the raw severity label without normalizing to a common CVSS-anchored scale.
detection_signal: Azure Defender: CRITICAL vulnerability on vm-vehicle-datalake-001 — CRITICAL severity as reported by cloud provider
ground_truth: CVE has CVSS 9.1. Under the aggregator's normalized severity schema (Critical: >=9.5, High: 7.0-9.4), this is a HIGH finding. Microsoft's Critical threshold starts at 9.0, creating a one-tier inflation artifact.
remediation_impact: CRITICAL findings in this environment trigger a mandatory 24-hour emergency patching SLA. Incorrect classification wastes 4-6 hours of on-call engineer time and may delay genuinely critical items.

scenario: IAM role ota-orchestrator-prod has policies granting S3:GetObject, S3:PutObject, and ECR:BatchGetImage on wildcard resources. CSPM flags this as an overprivileged role with broad S3 and ECR access. The role has an IAM Permission Boundary attached that restricts effective permissions to only the ota-firmware-* S3 prefix and the production ECR repository, preventing any access outside these scopes even if policies are expanded.
why_misclassified: EC-15: permission boundary compensating control not evaluated. The scanner reports the attached policy's stated permissions but does not compute the effective permissions after applying the Permission Boundary's deny-based restrictions.
detection_signal: IAM role ota-orchestrator-prod has wildcard S3 and ECR permissions — HIGH: OTA firmware role may access arbitrary S3 data
ground_truth: Permission Boundary arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:policy/ota-boundary restricts effective S3 access to s3:::ota-firmware-* prefix only. Wildcard policy statements are rendered harmless by the boundary.
remediation_impact: Rewriting the attached policies to match the boundary exactly is hygiene work only — no security improvement. Automated tightening could break future legitimate OTA firmware key paths.

scenario: EBS volume vol-0abc123456 attached to a vehicle-in-the-loop simulation EC2 instance is unencrypted. CSPM reports HIGH severity encryption gap. The EC2 instance is an ephemeral simulation node that is auto-terminated after each 4-hour simulation cycle. The volume contains only synthetic vehicle sensor data generated for HIL testing; it contains no production vehicle data or PII.
why_misclassified: EC-10: ephemeral workload lifecycle not considered. The scanner does not correlate volume lifetime with EC2 instance auto-termination schedules or evaluate data sensitivity tags on the volume.
detection_signal: EBS volume vol-0abc123456 is unencrypted — HIGH: automotive simulation infrastructure data at rest not encrypted
ground_truth: Volume lives for 4 hours maximum, contains only synthetic HIL test data, and is destroyed with the EC2 instance. Data has no sensitivity classification. Encryption adds I/O latency that distorts real-time simulation timing.
remediation_impact: Enabling EBS encryption on HIL simulation volumes increases I/O latency by 5-8%, causing timing jitter in sensor simulation loops that invalidates ISO 21434 test reproducibility requirements.

scenario: CSPM reports 4 separate HIGH findings for the same S3 bucket vehicle-logs-prod: missing bucket encryption, missing bucket versioning, missing access logging, and missing MFA delete. Cross-region replication to us-west-2 duplicates all 4 findings for the replica bucket, generating 8 total findings. The primary bucket's configuration already satisfies all 4 controls; the replica bucket inherits configuration but the scanner treats each region's findings independently.
why_misclassified: EC-38: cross-region replication creates duplicate findings. The scanner evaluates each regional bucket endpoint independently, failing to identify that bucket-west is a replication target of bucket-east which has all controls satisfied.
detection_signal: S3 bucket vehicle-logs-prod-replica missing encryption, versioning, access logging, MFA delete — HIGH x4: automotive compliance controls absent
ground_truth: vehicle-logs-prod (primary) has all controls enabled. vehicle-logs-prod-replica is a read-only CRR target that inherits the same configuration. CRR replica buckets use the source bucket's encryption; the API response differs for replicas causing false reads.
remediation_impact: Attempting to configure the replica bucket independently would conflict with CRR replication settings and potentially break the DR replication relationship.

scenario: GCP Cloud SQL instance vin-lookup-prod has authorized networks 0.0.0.0/0 configured, flagged as CRITICAL by CSPM. Investigation reveals the database contains only a static VIN prefix-to-manufacturer lookup table — publicly available data derived from the open NHTSA VIN database. No vehicle owner PII, diagnostic data, or proprietary information is stored. The broad access is a legacy configuration from when the database served a public API.
why_misclassified: EC-20: empty vault / non-sensitive data. Scanner cannot assess data sensitivity of Cloud SQL contents from the configuration API alone. The CRITICAL flag assumes worst-case PII exposure.
detection_signal: Cloud SQL instance vin-lookup-prod accessible from 0.0.0.0/0 — CRITICAL: production vehicle database exposed to internet
ground_truth: Database contains only public NHTSA VIN prefix data (WMI codes and manufacturer mappings). All data is publicly available from NHTSA API. No vehicle owner information, no proprietary data.
remediation_impact: While tightening access is good hygiene, the urgency is low given the non-sensitive public data. Immediate remediation should be scheduled, not emergency-patched.

scenario: Security group for the vehicle command & control API allows HTTPS (443) from 0.0.0.0/0. CSPM reports HIGH network exposure for a vehicle remote command endpoint. The entire fleet management API is behind AWS WAF with AWS Shield Advanced enabled, geo-blocking all regions except countries where vehicles are sold, and rate-limiting to 10 requests/second per IP to prevent command replay attacks.
why_misclassified: EC-05: WAF-shielded endpoint. The scanner evaluates the EC2/ALB security group rules without correlating the WAF WebACL that provides the actual access control layer above the SG.
detection_signal: ALB security group sg-fleet-cmd-api allows TCP 443 from 0.0.0.0/0 — HIGH: vehicle command API accessible from unrestricted internet
ground_truth: AWS WAF WebACL enforces geo-blocking (8 countries), rate limiting (10 req/s), and OWASP Top 10 rules. Shield Advanced provides DDoS protection. The SG 0.0.0.0/0 rule is necessary for ALB to receive WAF-filtered traffic.
remediation_impact: Restricting the ALB security group to specific CIDRs is impossible when WAF is the entry point — WAF forwards from AWS infrastructure IPs. This is the standard AWS WAF architecture.

scenario: Azure SQL Database connected-vehicle-telemetry does not have Transparent Data Encryption enabled via Azure-managed keys. CSPM reports HIGH encryption gap in a TISAX-scoped system. However, the application layer implements AES-256 field-level encryption for all PII fields before data reaches the database, using keys stored in Azure Key Vault. Data at rest in SQL is already encrypted at the application layer.
why_misclassified: EC-13: application-layer encryption compensating control. The scanner checks for TDE configuration via Azure API but cannot detect application-layer encryption implemented above the database layer.
detection_signal: Azure SQL vehicle-telemetry-db lacks TDE — HIGH: TISAX-scope vehicle data unencrypted at rest
ground_truth: Application encrypts all PII (VIN, owner ID, location) using AES-256 before INSERT. Key management uses Azure Key Vault with TISAX-certified HSM backing. Data at rest is encrypted at application layer even without TDE.
remediation_impact: Enabling TDE adds encryption overhead on a database that is already encrypted at the field level. TDE would add double-encryption with minimal security benefit but measurable query performance overhead.

scenario: CSPM detects root account activity in the HAEA-Automotive-Prod AWS account and reports CRITICAL IAM finding. The root account was used once to configure AWS GovCloud account linking, which is a task that legitimately requires root credentials. The access was by the designated TISAX break-glass root account holder using hardware MFA, logged, and reviewed by the CISO team.
why_misclassified: EC-28: break-glass role usage. The scanner cannot distinguish between unauthorized root access and documented break-glass procedures. All root account usage generates identical alerts regardless of authorization context.
detection_signal: Root account login detected in HAEA-Automotive-Prod — CRITICAL: unauthorized privileged access in ISO 21434 production environment
ground_truth: Root access was authorized for AWS GovCloud account linking per AWS documentation requirements. Access was by the TISAX-designated break-glass custodian with hardware MFA. Session was recorded and reviewed within 2 hours per TISAX IR-1 procedures.
remediation_impact: No remediation required. The break-glass access was documented and closed within the required window. Alert should be acknowledged and correlated with the change record.

scenario: Elastic IP eipalloc-0abc123 is flagged as unattached and presenting a MEDIUM exposure risk due to reserved but unassociated public IP. This EIP is reserved for the HAEA DR failover NAT Gateway and is intentionally unattached during normal operations. The EIP is only associated when the primary region fails and the DR runbook activates the failover NAT Gateway.
why_misclassified: EC-07: orphaned IP lifecycle context. The scanner sees an unattached EIP as a misconfiguration. It cannot determine whether the EIP is an intentional reserved DR resource or a genuinely orphaned asset.
detection_signal: Elastic IP eipalloc-0abc123 is unattached — MEDIUM: unused public IP increases attack surface in automotive production account
ground_truth: EIP is reserved for the us-west-2 DR NAT Gateway per the HAEA DR runbook. Attaching it during normal operations would expose the DR NAT Gateway unnecessarily. The EIP has a Name tag 'dr-natgw-failover-reserved'.
remediation_impact: Releasing this EIP would break the DR failover runbook. During an actual DR event, EIP reacquisition may not return the same IP, causing DNS propagation delays of 5-30 minutes during a failover.

scenario: Azure Defender for Containers is disabled on subscription HAEA-Automotive-Blue-v2. CSPM reports HIGH: monitoring gap in automotive production. This subscription is the blue environment in a blue-green deployment; it is currently inactive (green is serving traffic). The subscription maintains the previous application version and is in standby mode pending canary promotion validation, not receiving production traffic.
why_misclassified: EC-12: blue-green inactive environment. The scanner cannot distinguish between an active production subscription and a standby blue-green deployment slot.
detection_signal: Defender for Containers disabled on HAEA-Automotive-Blue-v2 — HIGH: TISAX-scope containers unmonitored in production subscription
ground_truth: HAEA-Automotive-Blue-v2 is the inactive blue deployment. No production traffic is routed to it. Defender is enabled on HAEA-Automotive-Green-v2 (active). Blue will receive Defender coverage when it becomes active in the next deployment rotation.
remediation_impact: Enabling Defender on the inactive blue subscription adds $400/month in monitoring costs for an environment that receives no traffic. More importantly, it complicates the deployment automation that manages Defender state transitions.

scenario: Lambda function connected-car-telemetry-processor is flagged for CVE-2023-44487 (HTTP/2 Rapid Reset, CVSS 7.5). This CVE was initially rated CRITICAL but was later revised to MEDIUM after NVD analysis and multiple vendors issued REJECTED/DISPUTED status for specific implementation contexts. The Lambda's HTTP client library vendor issued a VEX attestation stating this CVE does not apply to their implementation.
why_misclassified: EC-46: withdrawn or vendor-disputed CVE. The scanner uses the original NVD entry severity without checking for CVE status updates, vendor VEX files, or CVSS score revisions published after initial disclosure.
detection_signal: Lambda connected-car-telemetry-processor contains CVE-2023-44487 — CRITICAL: HTTP/2 Rapid Reset DoS in vehicle telemetry processor
ground_truth: CVE was revised to MEDIUM (CVSS 7.5). The HTTP client library vendor issued VEX attestation NOT_AFFECTED for this CVE. NVD entry updated with analysis notes. Scanner uses stale initial severity.
remediation_impact: Emergency patching response triggered for a CVE that does not apply to this implementation wastes 3-4 hours of on-call time and risks introducing regression from unnecessary dependency changes.

scenario: GCP firewall rule allows SSH (22) from the corporate VPN CIDR 10.10.0.0/16 to ADAS compute nodes. CSPM applies the EC-52 automotive sub-system severity multiplier and escalates from MEDIUM to CRITICAL because the tagged workload type is adas-compute. The VPN-restricted SSH access is a standard DevOps access pattern and the ADAS nodes run simulation workloads, not vehicle safety-critical software in production vehicles.
why_misclassified: EC-52: automotive sub-system severity multiplier applied without sub-system criticality validation. The multiplier is intended for V2X command channels and vehicle safety controls, not cloud simulation infrastructure.
detection_signal: Firewall allows SSH from corporate VPN to ADAS compute — CRITICAL: automotive safety subsystem SSH access via multiplied severity (EC-52)
ground_truth: ADAS compute nodes run simulation workloads on cloud VMs. They are not connected to production vehicles, V2X networks, or physical ADAS hardware. Standard corporate VPN SSH access is appropriate for these development simulation instances.
remediation_impact: Misapplied critical classification triggers emergency patching SLA. Correct severity is MEDIUM — SSH from VPN to cloud VMs is standard and appropriate here.

scenario: S3 bucket vehicle-crash-test-raw lacks default encryption. CSPM flags HIGH for unencrypted automotive safety data. The bucket is used to store raw crash test simulation outputs from FEA (Finite Element Analysis) runs — pure numerical physics output (stress tensors, deformation vectors) with no PII, no proprietary production designs, and no vehicle identification. All data was synthetically generated for NCAP simulation validation.
why_misclassified: EC-21: synthetic/non-sensitive data misclassified as sensitive based on name heuristics. The scanner infers automotive safety criticality from the bucket name 'crash-test' without evaluating the actual data classification tag (sensitivity=synthetic-public).
detection_signal: S3 bucket vehicle-crash-test-raw lacks encryption — HIGH: automotive safety test data stored unencrypted
ground_truth: Bucket contains only synthetic FEA numerical output. Data tagged sensitivity=synthetic-public. No PII, no production designs, no proprietary IP. Encryption adds 15% I/O overhead on multi-GB FEA output files.
remediation_impact: Enabling encryption on this bucket for purely synthetic numerical data provides no security benefit while adding I/O overhead to large FEA file operations.

scenario: NSG for the vehicle software build pipeline VMs allows unrestricted outbound to the internet. CSPM flags this as MEDIUM risk for potential data exfiltration. The outbound internet access is required for fetching open-source build dependencies from NPM/Maven/GitHub. An Azure Firewall in front of the subnet enforces FQDN-based egress filtering allowing only pre-approved package registries and CDNs.
why_misclassified: EC-16: edge-shielded network. The NSG appears permissive but Azure Firewall provides application-layer egress control. The scanner evaluates the NSG rules without detecting the Azure Firewall policy applied to the subnet's default route.
detection_signal: NSG allows unrestricted outbound on vnet-build-pipeline — MEDIUM: automotive build infrastructure may exfiltrate intellectual property
ground_truth: Azure Firewall enforces FQDN egress rules allowing only registry.npmjs.com, repo.maven.apache.org, and github.com/download paths. All other outbound is blocked. NSG permissiveness is intentional to allow firewall policy management.
remediation_impact: Adding NSG egress rules would conflict with Azure Firewall's policy model — the recommended architecture is to handle egress at the firewall layer, not duplicate rules at the NSG layer.

scenario: Lambda function vehicle-event-router running on the provided.al2023 managed runtime is flagged for a CVE in the Node.js runtime. The Lambda is deployed as a Go binary using the custom runtime (bootstrap), not Node.js. AWS manages the provided.al2023 runtime layer; the Node.js CVE is in an AWS-managed layer that is not loaded for Go-based custom runtime Lambdas.
why_misclassified: EC-36: Lambda managed runtime vs customer code CVE. Scanner identifies CVEs in the Lambda execution environment layer generically without determining which runtime handler is actually loaded. Go custom runtime does not instantiate the Node.js layer.
detection_signal: Lambda vehicle-event-router — HIGH: Node.js CVE in Lambda execution environment for automotive event routing
ground_truth: Lambda uses Go custom runtime (provided.al2023). The Node.js CVE is in an AWS-managed layer that is not invoked for this function. Remediation responsibility lies with AWS for managed runtime CVEs, not the customer.
remediation_impact: Customer has no ability to patch AWS-managed runtime layers. Filing unnecessary support tickets and triggering escalations for an AWS-owned CVE in a layer that is not used is wasted effort.

scenario: S3 bucket containing production connected vehicle telemetry has a tag suppress-cspm=true. CSPM suppresses all findings for this bucket. The bucket has a genuine misconfiguration: public read access was inadvertently enabled during a Terraform refactor. The suppression tag was applied broadly across the HAEA bucket fleet to reduce noise during a migration project and was never removed from production buckets.
why_misclassified: EC-49: tag-based suppression masking a real production issue. This is a false negative — not a false positive. The suppression tag hides a legitimate HIGH finding. The tag was applied to dev/staging buckets but inadvertently also applied to production.
detection_signal: [SUPPRESSED] S3 bucket vehicle-telemetry-prod public access enabled — suppressed via tag suppress-cspm=true
ground_truth: This IS a real finding. The bucket has public read access enabled, exposing aggregated vehicle telemetry. The CSPM suppression is incorrect — this is a production bucket with sensitive data that should not be suppressed.
remediation_impact: Actual remediation required: remove public access block, audit suppression tags on all production buckets, implement tag governance to prevent prod suppression. Immediate fix needed.

scenario: GKE cluster kia-telemetry-us-central1 is running Kubernetes 1.27, which is past its upstream EOL. CSPM reports MEDIUM for running a sunset Kubernetes version. GKE Extended Support is active on this cluster, providing continued security patches from Google through 2025-Q3. The cluster is scheduled for upgrade in the next quarterly maintenance window already approved by the HAEA change board.
why_misclassified: EC-11: sunset lifecycle with active vendor extended support. The scanner evaluates against upstream Kubernetes EOL dates without checking GKE Extended Support status or upgrade schedules already planned.
detection_signal: GKE cluster running Kubernetes 1.27 (EOL) — MEDIUM: automotive telemetry cluster on unsupported version
ground_truth: Google Extended Support for GKE 1.27 is active and provides security patches. Cluster upgrade to 1.29 is scheduled for Q3 2025 maintenance window (CR-2025-0412). No unpatched CVEs exist under GKE Extended Support.
remediation_impact: Forced immediate upgrade outside the approved change window violates the HAEA change management process and risks breaking deployed workloads without proper testing.

scenario: ECS task for the ADAS feature extraction pipeline contains Python package opencv-python flagged for CVE-2023-4863 (libwebp heap buffer overflow). The ADAS pipeline processes camera image frames from simulation datasets only — it never loads WebP images. The feature extraction code explicitly calls cv2.imread() with only JPEG and PNG inputs. The vulnerable WebP codec path in libwebp is never triggered.
why_misclassified: EC-03: disabled feature code path. The CVE affects WebP image decoding functionality that is present in the library but never invoked by the application code. The scanner cannot trace execution paths through OpenCV's codec dispatch table.
detection_signal: ECS task adas-feature-extraction contains CVE-2023-4863 — HIGH: automotive ADAS pipeline vulnerable to image processing memory corruption
ground_truth: The pipeline processes only JPEG and PNG frames. WebP codec in libwebp is not invoked. CVE-2023-4863 requires processing a malicious WebP image — no such input can reach this pipeline.
remediation_impact: While updating opencv-python is advisable for hygiene, the urgency is low given no WebP code path is active. Forced updates during active pipeline runs risk simulation output inconsistency.

scenario: Azure NSG allows TCP 3389 (RDP) from the corporate IP range during a 4-hour window. CSPM detects RDP open and reports HIGH. The access window is a scheduled maintenance warm-up period for deploying a new vehicle telemetry processing VM during a planned change window. RDP is only open during the 4-hour deployment window and is auto-closed by an Azure Automation runbook.
why_misclassified: EC-23: maintenance warm-up window. The scanner runs hourly and happened to scan during the legitimate maintenance window. No mechanism exists to correlate CSPM findings with approved change windows.
detection_signal: NSG allows RDP from corporate IP to vehicle telemetry VM — HIGH: management port exposed on TISAX-scope infrastructure
ground_truth: RDP access was open during an approved 4-hour change window (CR-2025-0788). Azure Automation runbook auto-closes RDP after deployment completion. Access was limited to corporate IP /24 and required MFA.
remediation_impact: CSPM alert was acknowledged and documented against the change record. No remediation needed — the port was already auto-closed by the automation before security team review.

scenario: Kinesis stream vehicle-telemetry-realtime uses server-side encryption with the default AWS managed key (aws/kinesis). CSPM reports HIGH because the TISAX policy requires CMK encryption. However, the specific TISAX assessment for this account only requires AWS-managed SSE for streaming data, not customer-managed keys. The policy misconfiguration is a CSPM rule overapplication of a stricter tier's requirement.
why_misclassified: EC-50: CSP enhanced controls inflating severity. The CSPM tool applies the TISAX AL3 requirement (CMK) to all TISAX-tagged resources, but this account is only assessed at TISAX AL2 where AWS SSE is sufficient.
detection_signal: Kinesis stream vehicle-telemetry-realtime uses AWS managed key — HIGH: TISAX-scope streaming data must use CMK encryption
ground_truth: This account holds TISAX AL2 assessment. AL2 requires data encryption at rest — fulfilled by aws/kinesis SSE. AL3 CMK requirement applies to a different account tier. CSPM policy templates are not tiered by TISAX assessment level.
remediation_impact: Migrating from AWS-managed to CMK encryption for Kinesis requires stream recreation with downtime. The change provides no compliance benefit for the AL2 assessment level.

scenario: IAM user vehicle-pipeline-svc has MFA disabled. CSPM reports HIGH for TISAX-scope IAM user without MFA. This is a service account used only for programmatic access by the vehicle data pipeline. The account has no console access, only API keys. The account has hardware MFA configured at the API key issuance process — an SCP in the HAEA OU requires STS session tokens, effectively requiring the pipeline to use assume-role with MFA token injection at the automation layer.
why_misclassified: EC-14: hardware MFA compensating control at automation layer. The scanner checks the IAM user's MFA device configuration directly but doesn't evaluate the SCP-enforced assume-role chain that injects MFA context.
detection_signal: IAM user vehicle-pipeline-svc has no MFA device — HIGH: TISAX-scope service account lacks MFA
ground_truth: Service account uses API key + SCP-enforced assume-role with TOTP MFA injected by the automation framework. Effective MFA requirement is enforced. Console access is blocked by policy. Direct-key API calls are denied by the SCP.
remediation_impact: Enabling virtual MFA on a headless service account is unmanageable (TOTP seeds cannot be used in automation). The existing SCP+assume-role pattern is the AWS-recommended approach for service account MFA.

scenario: EKS pod adas-sensor-calibration runs with privileged=true flag, flagged HIGH by CSPM. The pod requires privileged mode to access USB-connected calibration hardware attached to EC2 bare metal instances used for ADAS sensor calibration workflows. OPA Gatekeeper policy on the cluster restricts privileged=true to only pods in the adas-calibration namespace, and these nodes are not accessible from the general workload network.
why_misclassified: EC-31: admission controller compensating for RBAC. OPA Gatekeeper scopes privileged containers to a specific namespace with restricted network access. Scanner reports the privilege flag without considering the namespace-scoped admission policy.
detection_signal: EKS pod adas-sensor-calibration running with privileged=true — HIGH: automotive ADAS infrastructure has privileged container
ground_truth: Privileged mode is required for USB hardware access on bare metal nodes. OPA Gatekeeper restricts this flag to the adas-calibration namespace only. Nodes are on a separate network segment with no lateral movement path to production workloads.
remediation_impact: Removing privileged mode breaks ADAS sensor calibration workflows that require direct hardware access. OPA Gatekeeper provides the required compensating control to scope this to dedicated nodes.

scenario: Container image vehicle-ml-inference:v1.4 is flagged for CVE-2024-5535 (OpenSSL BN_check_prime, CVSS 7.4) in the base image layer. The container runs a TensorRT model inference service. The vulnerable OpenSSL function is only exercised during certificate validation at connection establishment. The container's network connections are internal-only to an istio service mesh using pre-validated mTLS; OpenSSL's BN_check_prime is only called during cert chain validation which is handled by the sidecar proxy, not the container itself.
why_misclassified: EC-02: CVE in build/base layer, not runtime execution path. The vulnerability is in OpenSSL present in the image but the specific vulnerable function (BN_check_prime) is called by the Istio sidecar proxy, not the ML inference application code.
detection_signal: ECR image vehicle-ml-inference:v1.4 contains CVE-2024-5535 — HIGH: OpenSSL vulnerability in automotive ML inference pipeline
ground_truth: OpenSSL is present in the base image layer but the ML application binary does not make direct TLS calls. TLS termination is handled by the Istio envoy sidecar which uses a separately maintained OpenSSL build.
remediation_impact: Rebuilding the image for a base-layer CVE where the vulnerable code path is handled by the service mesh sidecar provides minimal security improvement while introducing rebuild/testing overhead.

scenario: Distroless container image for the V2X message broker contains 17 CVEs reported by GCP Artifact Analysis. All CVEs require shell access to exploit (RCE via shell injection, privilege escalation via SUID binaries). The image uses gcr.io/distroless/base which contains no shell, no package manager, and no OS userland. None of the 17 CVEs can be exploited in a containerized distroless environment.
why_misclassified: EC-29: distroless image CVE with AV:L attack vector that is unexploitable without shell access. CVSS AV:L requires local shell access as a prerequisite. Distroless images eliminate this attack vector entirely.
detection_signal: Artifact Registry image v2x-broker:v2.1 has 17 HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerabilities — scanner flags automotive communication infrastructure as critically vulnerable
ground_truth: All 17 CVEs require AV:L (local shell access) or exploit SUID/shell utilities. Distroless base image has no shell or OS binaries. The attack vector prerequisites cannot be satisfied in this runtime environment.
remediation_impact: Attempting to patch these CVEs in a distroless context is impossible — distroless images are minimal by design. These CVEs are definitively unexploitable in this container configuration.

scenario: GCP service account telemetry-bq-loader@kia-data.iam.gserviceaccount.com has roles/bigquery.dataEditor bound at the project level, flagged as overprivileged. This is a headless service account used exclusively by a Dataflow pipeline that writes processed vehicle telemetry to BigQuery. No human user can assume this SA; it is only usable by the Dataflow job service identity with Workload Identity Federation.
why_misclassified: EC-26: headless SA with no human-assumable scope. The scanner flags the broad BigQuery role without checking whether the SA has any human principal bindings or whether it is restricted to Workload Identity Federation only.
detection_signal: Service account telemetry-bq-loader has project-level BigQuery Editor — HIGH: automotive telemetry service account overprivileged
ground_truth: SA is bound exclusively to the Dataflow service identity via WIF. No IAM member can impersonate this SA via key or impersonation — only the Dataflow job's workload identity can use it. The BigQuery Editor role is required for the Dataflow write operations.
remediation_impact: Scoping to dataset-level would require significant Dataflow pipeline reconfiguration. The WIF restriction provides effective isolation equivalent to dataset-level scoping.

scenario: SBOM for the connected vehicle SDK container lists protobuf-java 3.21.7 as a dependency, flagged with CVE-2022-3509 (CVSS 7.5, protobuf message parsing DoS). SBOM analysis shows this package as a dependency of grpc-java test utilities. The SBOM includes all declared artifacts including test scope; the production container only bundles main scope dependencies, and protobuf-java test utilities are never imported into the runtime JAR.
why_misclassified: EC-44: SBOM never-imported package. The SBOM was generated from the full project dependency tree including test scope. The scanner treats all SBOM entries as runtime components without distinguishing production vs test scope.
detection_signal: SBOM entry protobuf-java 3.21.7 CVE-2022-3509 — HIGH: vehicle SDK communication library DoS vulnerability
ground_truth: protobuf-java is a testImplementation-scoped dependency in Gradle. It is not included in the production JAR or container image filesystem. Runtime scanning of the deployed container image confirms the package is absent.
remediation_impact: Forcing upgrade of a test-scope transitive dependency has no production security impact and requires regression testing of unit tests.

scenario: S3 bucket haea-ota-dist-prod has a public ACL. CSPM reports HIGH data exposure. This bucket distributes firmware OTA packages to vehicles globally. A VPC endpoint policy for S3 in the internal development VPC has an explicit Deny condition preventing internal hosts from bypassing signed URL requirements. All external access requires pre-signed URLs generated by the OTA signing service with 15-minute expiry.
why_misclassified: EC-18: VPC endpoint deny policy as compensating control. The scanner sees the public bucket configuration but does not evaluate the VPC endpoint policy that adds access control for internal paths, nor the pre-signed URL requirement for external access.
detection_signal: S3 bucket haea-ota-dist-prod has public access enabled — HIGH: automotive OTA distribution contains publicly accessible firmware
ground_truth: Firmware packages are intentionally distributable to vehicles with pre-signed URLs (15-min TTL). Firmware binaries are signed with RSA-4096. Even if downloaded without authorization, unsigned firmware is rejected by the vehicle's secure boot chain.
remediation_impact: Making the bucket private would break the OTA distribution architecture. All vehicle-destined firmware requires internet-reachable signed URLs. Secure boot in vehicles provides the actual security guarantee.

scenario: EKS pod spec for the ADAS model deployment pipeline contains an init container with a CVE-affected version of kubectl (CVE-2023-2727, CVSS 6.5, container escape via ephemeral containers). The init container runs once during pod startup to pre-fetch model weights from S3, then exits. The CVE is only exploitable during steady-state pod operation via the Kubernetes API — it cannot be triggered against an already-terminated init container.
why_misclassified: EC-30: init container CVE that is never exploitable in steady state. The vulnerable init container exits after the startup task completes. CVE-2023-2727 requires the container to be running and accessible via kubectl exec.
detection_signal: EKS pod init container uses vulnerable kubectl — HIGH: automotive ADAS pipeline init container with container escape CVE
ground_truth: The init container runs for <30 seconds during pod startup to fetch S3 model weights, then exits. Once exited, it cannot be targeted by the CVE exploit which requires an active container process.
remediation_impact: While updating kubectl in the init container image is advisable hygiene, the exploit window is limited to <30 seconds at pod startup only — not a steady-state risk.

scenario: Azure Function app processing vehicle warranty claims contains log4j-core 2.14.1 (CVE-2021-44228, Log4Shell). Code analysis reveals that the warranty processing code uses SLF4J API with Logback as the binding, not Log4j. Log4j-core is present as a transitive dependency of a DB2 JDBC driver but is never instantiated — the actual logging implementation loaded at runtime is Logback.
why_misclassified: EC-04: dead code path. Log4j-core is present in the classpath but the JVM logger factory binds to the Logback implementation. Log4j's LogManager.getLogger() is never called by the application or any active transitive dependency.
detection_signal: Azure Function vehicle-warranty-processor contains Log4Shell CVE-2021-44228 — HIGH: TISAX-scope function vulnerable to critical RCE
ground_truth: SLF4J binds to Logback at runtime (logback-classic is on the classpath). Log4j-core is present but the logging factory never initializes Log4j. JNDI lookup vulnerability in Log4j cannot be triggered as Log4j is not the active logging backend.
remediation_impact: While removing the unused Log4j dependency is correct hygiene, the critical urgency is unwarranted. Runtime confirmation that Logback is the active logger should be documented before emergency patching.

scenario: CSPM reports a NEW HIGH finding: a service principal gained Contributor role on the vehicle platform resource group. Security team investigates and finds the role was assigned 3 weeks ago during a planned infrastructure deployment. The CSPM scan was paused during a system migration and when scanning resumed, all changes during the pause period appear as NEW findings with current timestamps.
why_misclassified: EC-48: timezone/scan gap mismatch creating false NEW findings. The CSPM tool tracks finding state based on scan deltas. A 3-week scan gap causes all accumulated configuration states to appear as new changes in the resumption scan.
detection_signal: NEW: Service principal gained Contributor on vehicle-platform-rg — HIGH: TISAX-scope resource group permission change detected
ground_truth: Role assignment is 3 weeks old, made during approved change CR-2025-0456. The NEW classification is a CSPM scan-gap artifact. The role assignment is documented and reviewed.
remediation_impact: No remediation required. The finding should be correlated with the change record and acknowledged. CSPM scan continuity should be improved to prevent gap-induced false new findings.

scenario: DynamoDB table vehicle-session-tokens does not have CMK (customer managed key) encryption configured. CSPM reports HIGH: automotive session data lacks required encryption. DynamoDB encrypts all data at rest by default using AWS owned keys — this is not an absence of encryption but an absence of CMK specifically. The table contains session tokens with 15-minute TTL; the data sensitivity does not warrant CMK overhead.
why_misclassified: EC-39: serverless 'no encryption' means missing CMK, not missing encryption. AWS DynamoDB encrypts all tables using AWS owned keys by default. The CSPM policy equates 'no CMK configured' with 'no encryption', which is incorrect.
detection_signal: DynamoDB table vehicle-session-tokens lacks encryption configuration — HIGH: automotive session management data unencrypted
ground_truth: DynamoDB automatically encrypts all data at rest using AWS owned keys. 'No CMK' means AWS manages the key, not that data is unencrypted. CMK is only required when key management control is needed (e.g., for data deletion guarantees).
remediation_impact: Enabling CMK on DynamoDB for 15-minute TTL session tokens adds key management overhead with no meaningful security improvement for this data type.

scenario: Cloud Run service kia-diagnostics-api uses a vendored fork of the go-jose JWT library. The scanner flags CVE-2023-48795 (Terrapin attack on SSH, CVSS 5.9) on the vendored copy. The vendored go-jose fork was patched 8 months ago by the HAEA platform team to fix an unrelated JWT clock skew issue, and that patch incidentally included the Terrapin fix from upstream.
why_misclassified: EC-42: vendored patched fork. The scanner matches the CVE against the declared version string (v2.6.0) without detecting that the vendored copy includes post-v2.6.0 patches applied directly to the vendor directory.
detection_signal: Cloud Run kia-diagnostics-api vendored go-jose v2.6.0 CVE-2023-48795 — HIGH: vehicle diagnostics API vulnerable to SSH Terrapin attack
ground_truth: The vendored go-jose fork includes the CVE-2023-48795 fix from upstream v2.6.1 applied as a patch. The vulnerable line of code is absent from the vendor directory. Version string is outdated but the patch is present.
remediation_impact: Upgrading the vendor reference to a newer version string is correct hygiene but not security-urgent — the fix is already applied. The upgrade should happen in the next sprint.

scenario: RDS snapshot rds:vehicle-diagnostics-test-2025-01 is flagged as publicly restorable — CRITICAL data exposure. The snapshot is from the vehicle-diagnostics-test database which contains only tokenized VIN data. Real VINs are replaced with format-preserving tokens before loading into the test database. The snapshot contains no genuine vehicle identifiers or owner PII — all values are tokenized synthetic data.
why_misclassified: EC-22: tokenization of sensitive fields makes exposure low-risk. The scanner detects the public snapshot without evaluating the tokenization status of the data. The snapshot name includes 'vehicle' which triggers the automotive sensitivity multiplier.
detection_signal: RDS snapshot rds:vehicle-diagnostics-test-2025-01 is publicly restorable — CRITICAL: automotive vehicle data exposed via public snapshot
ground_truth: Snapshot contains tokenized VINs and synthetic diagnostic data. No real VINs, no owner PII, no proprietary diagnostic codes. Tokenization uses format-preserving encryption with keys that are not present in the snapshot.
remediation_impact: Making the snapshot private is correct hygiene regardless of data sensitivity, but the CRITICAL urgency is unwarranted. Should be scheduled remediation, not emergency.

scenario: EKS CronJob vehicle-cert-rotation runs weekly to rotate mTLS certificates for the vehicle PKI infrastructure. The CronJob pod image contains a CVE in Python 3.11 (CVE-2023-24329, URL parsing bypass). The pod runs for approximately 90 seconds once per week, executes the cert rotation script, and then terminates. The CVE requires an attacker to pass a crafted URL to urllib.parse — the cert rotation script only makes API calls to AWS ACM PCA, not user-provided URLs.
why_misclassified: EC-33: ephemeral CronJob pod CVE. The attack surface is limited to a 90-second weekly execution window. Additionally, the CVE requires URL input from an untrusted source, which this script never receives.
detection_signal: EKS CronJob vehicle-cert-rotation pod CVE-2023-24329 — HIGH: automotive PKI certificate rotation vulnerable to URL parsing attack
ground_truth: CronJob runs 90 seconds/week. The vulnerable urllib.parse function is called only with hardcoded ACM PCA endpoint URLs, not user-supplied input. Attack window is <90s/week and the code path cannot receive malicious URL input.
remediation_impact: Updating the Python base image is low-urgency hygiene. The actual exploit scenario (untrusted URL input) is not achievable in this CronJob's runtime context.

scenario: CSPM flags HIGH for a security group allowing inbound from 10.0.0.0/8 on the Hyundai connected car platform. Security review reveals this security group was replaced 45 days ago during a network segmentation project. The resource still appears in CSPM scan results because the CSPM tool's inventory is cached and has not re-synced after the deletion. The security group no longer exists in the AWS account.
why_misclassified: EC-24: stale scan finding for deleted resource. The CSPM tool's asset inventory has a stale cache entry for a deleted security group. The resource was deleted 45 days ago but the finding persists in the CSPM console.
detection_signal: SecurityGroup sg-0stale123 allows inbound from 10.0.0.0/8 — HIGH: automotive connected platform broad internal access
ground_truth: Security group sg-0stale123 was deleted on 2025-01-15 during network segmentation project (CR-2025-0123). The resource does not exist. CSPM tool has a stale inventory cache entry.
remediation_impact: No remediation required — resource no longer exists. CSPM tool inventory resync needed to clear stale findings.

scenario: GKE pod for the vehicle tracking service has a CVE in the Envoy proxy sidecar (CVE-2024-23324, CVE-2024-23325, CVSS 7.5) related to HTTP/1.1 protocol handling. The Istio service mesh on this cluster enforces STRICT mTLS mode across all services in the vehicle-platform namespace. Both CVEs require plain HTTP/1.1 traffic to trigger — all traffic is TLS-encrypted via Istio mTLS, making the HTTP/1.1 code path unreachable.
why_misclassified: EC-32: sidecar proxy CVE with strict mTLS in effect. The CVEs require plain HTTP/1.1 input. With Istio STRICT mTLS, the Envoy sidecar only processes TLS-wrapped traffic. The vulnerable HTTP/1.1 parsing path is never reached.
detection_signal: GKE pod vehicle-tracker Envoy sidecar CVE-2024-23324 — HIGH: vehicle tracking infrastructure HTTP/1.1 vulnerability
ground_truth: Istio PeerAuthentication is set to STRICT mode in the vehicle-platform namespace. All sidecar traffic is mTLS. The HTTP/1.1 code path in Envoy is not reachable in STRICT mTLS mode.
remediation_impact: Upgrading Istio/Envoy is recommended practice but not urgent given the unreachable code path under STRICT mTLS. Upgrade should be planned for the next Istio release cycle.

scenario: Cloud Run service hyundai-diagnostics-api has --allow-unauthenticated flag, flagged HIGH for public access on automotive infrastructure. The project has an org policy constraint/run.allowedIngressSettings=internal-and-cloud-load-balancing applied, which overrides the service-level unauthenticated setting and restricts access to internal VPC and Cloud Load Balancing origins only. The org policy was applied after the service was initially deployed.
why_misclassified: EC-40: GCP Cloud Run org policy override. The scanner evaluates the Cloud Run service's IAM configuration (allow-unauthenticated) without checking the Organization Policy constraint that restricts actual ingress regardless of the IAM binding.
detection_signal: Cloud Run service hyundai-diagnostics-api allows unauthenticated — HIGH: automotive diagnostics API publicly accessible
ground_truth: Org policy constraints/run.allowedIngressSettings=internal-and-cloud-load-balancing prevents direct public access. The allow-unauthenticated binding is effectively overridden. Only Load Balancer traffic can reach the service.
remediation_impact: Removing the allow-unauthenticated flag is correct configuration hygiene but not urgently required given the org policy override. Should be cleaned up in the next Terraform apply.

scenario: ECR repository vehicle-telemetry-processor has images without Sigstore cosign signatures. CSPM reports HIGH for unsigned images in ISO 21434 scope. The EKS cluster uses Kyverno with a policy requiring cosign verification for all images from vehicle-* repositories. All images are signed using AWS Signer (not cosign), and the Kyverno policy validates AWS Signer signatures at admission time, rejecting any unsigned image.
why_misclassified: EC-35: image signing with admission enforcement using an alternative signing mechanism. The scanner checks for cosign signatures specifically but the images use AWS Signer. The admission controller (Kyverno) enforces signing regardless of the specific signing tool.
detection_signal: ECR image vehicle-telemetry-processor:v3.1 lacks cosign signature — HIGH: automotive telemetry container unsigned, no supply chain verification
ground_truth: Images are signed with AWS Signer. Kyverno policy verifies AWS Signer signatures at admission. Unsigned images are rejected by the admission controller before scheduling. Supply chain verification is enforced, using a different signing standard.
remediation_impact: Migrating from AWS Signer to cosign requires rebuilding all signing pipelines. Both provide equivalent image integrity guarantees. Forced migration creates unnecessary risk.

scenario: Lambda function vehicle-data-aggregator uses Python package cryptography 41.0.3 which is flagged for CVE-2023-49083 (NULL pointer dereference, CVSS 7.5). Analysis of the Lambda code shows it uses the cryptography package only for AES-256 encryption via Fernet. CVE-2023-49083 affects the PKCS#12 parsing code path, which requires loading a PKCS#12 file. This Lambda never processes PKCS#12 certificates and has no code path that calls the vulnerable function.
why_misclassified: EC-01: ghost package — library present but vulnerable function path is a dead code path. The CVSS score assumes the worst-case usage of the library; this Lambda uses only Fernet/AES which is not affected by the PKCS#12 CVE.
detection_signal: Lambda vehicle-data-aggregator cryptography 41.0.3 CVE-2023-49083 — CRITICAL: automotive data pipeline cryptography vulnerable to NULL pointer dereference
ground_truth: CVE-2023-49083 is in the PKCS#12 certificate loading code. This Lambda uses only Fernet symmetric encryption (AES-128-CBC). No PKCS#12 or X.509 certificate processing occurs. The vulnerable code path is never executed.
remediation_impact: Upgrading cryptography to 41.0.4 is good hygiene but the CRITICAL urgency is unwarranted for an unexploitable code path. Should be included in the next regular dependency update cycle.

scenario: S3 bucket haea-vehicle-telemetry-prod-archive has public access enabled but is completely suppressed in the CSPM tool via a tag suppress-findings=all applied during a pre-TISAX audit cleanup project 8 months ago. The bucket contains 6 months of raw vehicle telemetry including GPS traces, driver behavior scores, and VINs. The suppression tag was applied in error to a production bucket instead of the test bucket.
why_misclassified: EC-49: tag-based suppression masking a genuine CRITICAL production issue. The CSPM suppression tag was misapplied to a production bucket containing PII. No finding is generated so the real exposure is invisible.
detection_signal: [SUPPRESSED — NO FINDING GENERATED] Bucket tagged suppress-findings=all
ground_truth: Real CRITICAL finding. Bucket has public access enabled, contains vehicle GPS traces + VINs + driver behavior scores (GDPR/CCPA PII). Exposed for 8 months due to erroneous suppression tag.
remediation_impact: Immediate actions required: (1) remove public access block, (2) remove incorrect suppression tag, (3) conduct data exposure impact assessment, (4) evaluate GDPR notification obligation. Potential regulatory exposure.

scenario: Azure Defender reports LOW severity for a vulnerability on the HAEA vehicle platform VM. The CVE (CVE-2024-21338, CVSS 7.8) affects Windows kernel CLFS driver — a privilege escalation to SYSTEM that was actively exploited in the wild (CISA KEV listed). Microsoft's Defender severity scale rates this LOW based on their proprietary contextual factors, but the CVE's real-world exploitation and CISA KEV status make it HIGH in the aggregator's risk model.
why_misclassified: EC-47: CSP severity scale non-equivalence in reverse direction. Microsoft Defender downgraded the severity based on internal threat intelligence, but CISA KEV status and active exploitation evidence should override the low CSP rating.
detection_signal: Azure Defender: LOW severity CVE-2024-21338 on vm-haea-platform-001 — aggregator inherits LOW from cloud provider
ground_truth: CVE-2024-21338 is on CISA KEV list with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation. CVSS 7.8 privilege escalation to SYSTEM. Should be rated HIGH or CRITICAL by the aggregator regardless of Defender's contextual downgrade.
remediation_impact: Under-prioritized patching due to LOW severity label. This CVE was exploited by North Korean threat actors (Lazarus Group) for lateral movement in automotive supply chain targets in 2024.

scenario: Security group for the vehicle telematics ingestion endpoint allows SSH (port 22) from 10.0.0.0/8 (all private RFC1918). CSPM rates this LOW because the source is private IP ranges, not internet. However, the HAEA corporate VPN assigns addresses in 10.0.0.0/8 to all 12,000 employees globally. A single compromised employee device could pivot to SSH into the telematics ingestion EC2 fleet.
why_misclassified: EC-09: dev/internal inflation suppressed too aggressively. The scanner treats all RFC1918 source CIDRs as equivalent. A /8 covering all corporate VPN users is functionally much riskier than a specific jump-host /32.
detection_signal: SecurityGroup allows SSH from 10.0.0.0/8 — LOW: private IP range SSH access on telematics ingestion
ground_truth: 10.0.0.0/8 encompasses all 12,000 HAEA VPN users globally. A single compromised employee endpoint enables SSH to the vehicle telematics fleet. The CIDR breadth makes this a HIGH risk despite being RFC1918.
remediation_impact: SSH access should be restricted to the bastion host /32 only. Broad VPN SSH access to the telematics ingestion fleet violates least access and creates a significant lateral movement path.

scenario: IAM role connected-vehicle-lambda has an inline policy with Action: '*' on Resource: 'arn:aws:s3:::haea-vehicle-*'. CSPM rates this MEDIUM as 'wildcard action on specific prefix'. However, the S3 prefix haea-vehicle-* encompasses 47 production buckets including firmware signing keys, vehicle command authorization databases, and connected car PII stores. The wildcard action enables DeleteBucket, PutBucketPolicy, and ACL manipulation.
why_misclassified: EC-50: CSP enhanced severity controls suppressing what should be a toxic combination. Wildcard S3 action on a prefix covering critical automotive infrastructure should be CRITICAL, not MEDIUM. Resource specificity is oversold as a compensating control.
detection_signal: IAM role connected-vehicle-lambda Action:* on s3:::haea-vehicle-* — MEDIUM: scoped wildcard IAM policy
ground_truth: 47 production buckets match haea-vehicle-* including firmware signing, vehicle command authorization, and PII stores. Wildcard S3 action enables data destruction, bucket policy manipulation, and ACL-based exposure. This is CRITICAL.
remediation_impact: Immediate policy tightening required. Role should only have specific S3 actions (GetObject, PutObject) on the specific buckets it legitimately accesses.

scenario: HAEA has a multi-region CloudTrail configured in us-east-1 as the home region. The trail is set to multi-region=true, which appears to cover all regions. However, data events (S3 GetObject, Lambda Invoke) are only enabled for us-east-1. HAEA vehicle telematics workloads run in eu-west-1 (Korea-EU data residency requirement). Lambda invocations and S3 access in eu-west-1 generate no CloudTrail data events, creating an audit blindspot for TISAX.
why_misclassified: EC-38: cross-region scope limitation creating a genuine audit gap. The CSPM tool verifies CloudTrail is enabled and multi-region, rating it compliant. It does not verify that data event coverage extends to all workload regions.
detection_signal: [NO FINDING — CloudTrail shows multi-region=true]
ground_truth: Data event logging gap in eu-west-1. All S3 data access and Lambda invocations in eu-west-1 (Korean vehicle data EU residency region) are unlogged. TISAX requires complete activity logging. This is a genuine HIGH compliance gap.
remediation_impact: Enable data events in eu-west-1 or add a dedicated data event trail for the EU region. Without this, forensic investigation of any eu-west-1 data access incident is impossible.

scenario: Managed identity for the vehicle data processing VM has Contributor role on the HAEA resource group (MEDIUM finding in CSPM). A separate check also validates that Azure Policy assignments restrict what actions Contributor can take. CSPM sees the Contributor role + Policy assignment and downgrades to LOW. However, the Policy only restricts resource creation — it does not restrict the ability to exfiltrate existing data, modify Key Vault access policies, or modify existing resources.
why_misclassified: EC-15 in reverse: permission boundary only partially compensates. The CSPM treats any policy assignment as sufficient compensation, but the policy scope is limited to resource creation types and does not cover data access or secret exfiltration.
detection_signal: VM managed identity has Contributor on HAEA resource group — LOW: Azure Policy compensating control in place
ground_truth: Contributor + Key Vault Secrets User allows the VM identity to read all Key Vault secrets in the resource group. Azure Policy does not block data reads. This is HIGH: vehicle platform VM can read all secrets including vehicle command signing keys.
remediation_impact: Managed identity should be scoped to specific resource groups and specific roles. Contributor on the entire resource group violates least-privilege.

scenario: Lambda function vehicle-command-dispatcher has its OTA signing private key stored as a Lambda environment variable SIGNING_KEY_B64, base64-encoded. CSPM scans Lambda configurations but only checks for patterns matching common secret formats (AWS keys, connection strings). The base64-encoded RSA private key does not match any CSPM secret detection pattern. The key, if extracted, would allow signing arbitrary firmware packages accepted by all HAEA vehicles.
why_misclassified: EC-22: encoding hides what is actually a secret. The CSPM pattern matching for secrets does not detect base64-encoded private keys in environment variables unless they match known prefixes.
detection_signal: [NO FINDING — environment variable SIGNING_KEY_B64 not matched by secret detection patterns]
ground_truth: CRITICAL: RSA private key for vehicle firmware signing stored in Lambda environment variable as base64. Any Lambda execution role compromise exposes the signing key. Attacker with this key can sign malicious firmware accepted by all HAEA vehicles.
remediation_impact: Emergency: rotate signing key, move to AWS Secrets Manager with KMS CMK, audit all Lambda configurations for embedded keys. UNECE WP.29 requires secure key storage for OTA signing.

scenario: S3 bucket policy for haea-vehicle-pii-prod allows cross-account GetObject from account 987654321098. CSPM rates this LOW because both accounts share the HAEA AWS Organization. Security investigation reveals account 987654321098 is a recently onboarded third-party supplier (Tier-2 supplier for seat electronics) that was incorrectly invited into the HAEA AWS Organization. The account belongs to an external company, not HAEA's internal fleet.
why_misclassified: EC-27 reversed: intra-org trust assumption is wrong. CSPM correctly identifies same-organization accounts as trusted, but the organization has an incorrectly enrolled third-party account.
detection_signal: S3 cross-account access from HAEA-org account 987654321098 — LOW: intra-org trust
ground_truth: Account 987654321098 belongs to a Tier-2 automotive supplier incorrectly enrolled in the HAEA AWS Organization. This grants the supplier access to vehicle PII S3 data. Real HIGH finding.
remediation_impact: Remove the supplier account from the HAEA organization, revoke S3 bucket policy grant, audit what data was accessed. Initiate data breach assessment per GDPR Article 33.

scenario: A GCP firewall rule allow-all-internal-v2x was created 6 months ago to allow all TCP traffic within the v2x VPC network. CSPM scans were paused during the rule creation window and when scans resumed, the rule appeared as an existing baseline configuration and was not flagged as a deviation. The rule enables lateral movement from any compromised V2X node to all internal V2X infrastructure.
why_misclassified: EC-24: stale scan baseline incorporating a dangerous rule as 'known state'. The CSPM baseline was set after the problematic rule was created during a scan gap.
detection_signal: [NO FINDING — rule exists in baseline established after scan pause]
ground_truth: CRITICAL: allow-all-internal-v2x permits any-to-any TCP within the V2X network. Any compromised RSU or V2X node can move laterally to all V2X infrastructure including the vehicle command channel.
remediation_impact: Immediate rule removal required. Replace with specific rules allowing only documented V2X communication paths. Investigate whether lateral movement occurred during the 6-month exposure window.

scenario: The HAEA vehicle command API uses AWS WAF as the primary access control layer. CSPM validates the WAF is attached and active. Security team discovers that the EC2 security group allows direct access on port 8080 from 0.0.0.0/0, providing a WAF bypass path to the backend vehicle command API without passing through WAF rule evaluation.
why_misclassified: EC-05 reversed: WAF-shielded only in the intended path. The scanner validates WAF is attached to the CloudFront distribution but misses the direct EC2 security group exposure that bypasses the WAF entirely.
detection_signal: [NO WAF BYPASS FINDING — WAF attachment verified on CloudFront distribution]
ground_truth: HIGH: Port 8080 on vehicle command API EC2 instances is directly accessible, bypassing AWS WAF and all geo-blocking/rate-limiting controls. UNECE WP.29 vehicle command security controls are circumventable.
remediation_impact: Emergency: remove port 8080 from public SG, restrict EC2 access to ALB origin only. All UNECE WP.29 vehicle command security controls depend on the WAF being in the critical path.

scenario: Organization-level CloudTrail is enabled across all HAEA accounts. However, the S3 bucket receiving CloudTrail logs has a bucket policy that allows cloudtrail.amazonaws.com to write logs but also has a wildcard GetObject policy for all principals with assume-role. Investigation reveals the CloudTrail log bucket is inadvertently readable by all HAEA IAM roles, exposing the audit trail to any compromised role.
why_misclassified: Logging exists but is improperly secured. The CSPM checks for log presence, not log confidentiality.
detection_signal: [NO FINDING — CloudTrail org trail active, logs being written to S3]
ground_truth: HIGH: CloudTrail audit logs are readable by any HAEA IAM role. An attacker with any valid IAM credential can read audit logs revealing infrastructure topology, IAM usage patterns, and investigation activities.
remediation_impact: Restrict CloudTrail S3 bucket to security team role only. Log confidentiality is critical for TISAX incident investigation procedures.

scenario: Azure Function for vehicle session management uses application-layer AES-256 encryption for all stored data. CSPM rates encryption as compliant. However, the encryption key is retrieved from an environment variable set by an Azure Logic App workflow. The Logic App fetches the key from an HTTP endpoint using HTTP (not HTTPS) due to a misconfigured connector, transmitting the encryption key in plaintext over the network.
why_misclassified: EC-13 in reverse: application-layer encryption is present but the key transport is insecure. The CSPM verifies that encryption is used but cannot trace the key lifecycle to detect the plaintext key retrieval path.
detection_signal: [NO FINDING — Azure Function uses application-layer AES-256 encryption]
ground_truth: HIGH: AES-256 encryption key transmitted over HTTP by Logic App connector. Any network position between Logic App and the key endpoint can observe the encryption key. TISAX requires encrypted key transport.
remediation_impact: Fix Logic App HTTP connector to use HTTPS. Rotate the compromised encryption key. Audit all Logic App connectors for insecure transport.

scenario: ECS task for vehicle firmware validation uses libcurl 8.4.0 (with CVE-2023-38545, CVSS 9.8, SOCKS5 heap overflow) with a runtime feature flag DISABLE_SOCKS5_PROXY=true. CSPM detects the feature flag and suppresses the CVE as EC-45 (disabled dependency). However, the flag only disables application-level SOCKS5 usage — the underlying libcurl still has the vulnerable SOCKS5 code compiled in, exploitable if any other code path enables SOCKS5.
why_misclassified: EC-45: feature flag disabled dependency — but the flag only disables application-level usage, not the library-level vulnerability. The scanner treats the feature flag as a full compensating control.
detection_signal: [SUPPRESSED via EC-45 — DISABLE_SOCKS5_PROXY feature flag active]
ground_truth: HIGH: libcurl 8.4.0 CVE-2023-38545 is fully present in the runtime binary. The feature flag disables the application's use of SOCKS5 but does not patch the library. Any code path directly calling curl_easy_setopt with CURLOPT_PROXYTYPE could trigger the overflow.
remediation_impact: Upgrade libcurl to 8.5.0+. Feature flags are not equivalent to patching for compiled C libraries.

scenario: Root account login is detected in the HAEA-OTA-Prod account. CSPM has a suppression rule for root access when tagged with break-glass-authorized=true. The login was tagged with this marker by an automated playbook triggered when someone found the break-glass credentials checklist in an internal wiki. The actual break-glass custodian did not authorize the access — the credentials were used by an unauthorized actor.
why_misclassified: EC-28 reversed: the break-glass suppression rule can be triggered by automation, masking genuinely unauthorized root access. The CSPM suppression assumes the tag implies authorization, but the tag was applied by an automated rule, not a human custodian review.
detection_signal: [SUPPRESSED — root access tagged break-glass-authorized=true by automation]
ground_truth: CRITICAL: Unauthorized root account access in OTA production account. Root credentials were used by an unauthorized actor. The automated suppression rule masked the incident. OTA signing infrastructure may be compromised.
remediation_impact: Immediate incident response: revoke all active root sessions, rotate root credentials, review all actions taken during the session, notify CISO. Break-glass suppression automation must require human approval.

scenario: Cloud Run vehicle diagnostics service uses go-cve-dictionary for vulnerability database lookups. A CVE affecting the package was initially marked WITHDRAWN in NVD due to a data entry error, causing the scanner to suppress the finding. The CVE was subsequently reinstated in NVD with a CVSS 7.9 rating after error correction, but the scanner's CVE cache has not been refreshed and still shows WITHDRAWN status.
why_misclassified: EC-46 reversed: withdrawn CVE that was actually reinstated. The scanner suppresses withdrawn CVEs but does not detect when NVD reinstates a CVE after a data error correction.
detection_signal: [SUPPRESSED — CVE status: WITHDRAWN in scanner cache]
ground_truth: HIGH: CVE reinstated in NVD with CVSS 7.9. Scanner cache is stale. The vulnerability is real and present in the vehicle diagnostics service.
remediation_impact: Update scanner CVE database, patch affected package. Implement CVE status re-check for all suppressed-as-withdrawn findings on each scan cycle.

scenario: RDS instance kia-owner-pii-prod has publicly_accessible=false, which would make the EC-37 scanner check pass. However, the VPC was recently peered with an external partner network (a KIA dealer portal AWS account) with a route table entry pointing to the dealer VPC CIDR that covers the RDS subnet. The scanner sees publicly_accessible=false and reports compliant, but the effective network path now allows access from the dealer portal's VPC.
