why_misclassified: EC-37 extended: publicly_accessible=false but network topology creates reachability via VPC peering. The scanner checks the RDS attribute but does not trace VPC peering route tables to determine effective reachability.
detection_signal: [NO FINDING — RDS publicly_accessible=false]
ground_truth: HIGH: VPC peering with dealer portal creates network path to the RDS instance containing KIA owner PII. Owner PII database is reachable from the external partner network.
remediation_impact: Add RDS security group rule explicitly blocking dealer portal CIDR. Review all VPC peering routes to ensure PII databases are not reachable from partner networks.

scenario: Lambda function processing Korea-US vehicle data transfers uses pyjwt 2.4.0 with CVE-2022-29217 (algorithm confusion attack, CVSS 7.5). A separate test-scope package has identical naming patterns to pyjwt, and the EC-43 build-time dependency suppression regex incorrectly matches and suppresses the runtime pyjwt CVE finding.
why_misclassified: EC-43 suppression over-applied: the build-time dependency suppression rule regex matches both the genuine test package and the production pyjwt package. The suppression silences a real runtime JWT vulnerability.
detection_signal: [SUPPRESSED — matched EC-43 build-time dependency pattern]
ground_truth: HIGH: pyjwt 2.4.0 CVE-2022-29217 is a genuine runtime dependency processing JWT tokens in the Korea-US vehicle data transfer Lambda. Algorithm confusion attack can forge tokens. EC-43 suppression incorrectly applied.
remediation_impact: Upgrade pyjwt to 2.6.0+. Fix EC-43 suppression regex to not match runtime jwt libraries.

scenario: Azure NSG for the HAEA vehicle command backend has port 1883 (MQTT without TLS) open from the internal VNet range. The scanner applies EC-08 VPC-bounded logic and rates this LOW/suppressed because the source is the internal VNet. However, the MQTT broker on port 1883 accepts cleartext MQTT without authentication — any resource in the VNet can publish vehicle commands.
why_misclassified: EC-08 over-applied: VPC-bounded traffic is treated as low risk. Internal cleartext MQTT with no authentication is dangerous even from internal sources, especially given the vehicle command context.
detection_signal: [SUPPRESSED — NSG port 1883 from internal VNet only, EC-08 pattern]
ground_truth: HIGH: MQTT port 1883 (cleartext, no auth) accessible from entire VNet. Any compromised VM or container in the VNet can publish vehicle commands.
remediation_impact: Close port 1883, enforce mTLS on port 8883 only. Audit all internal network MQTT usage to ensure no cleartext fallback is in use.

scenario: GuardDuty is disabled in the HAEA-Vehicle-Blue account. CSPM applies EC-12 blue-green logic and suppresses this as the inactive deployment slot. However, the blue deployment became the active production slot 3 weeks ago during a deployment, and environment role tags were not updated after the swap.
why_misclassified: EC-12 reversed: environment role labels are stale after blue-green swap. The scanner trusts environment tags over actual traffic routing state.
detection_signal: [SUPPRESSED — account tagged environment=blue-inactive]
ground_truth: HIGH: GuardDuty is disabled in the currently active production account. The account receives all production vehicle platform traffic but has no threat detection coverage.
remediation_impact: Enable GuardDuty immediately in HAEA-Vehicle-Blue (now active). Update environment tags to reflect current deployment state. Implement tag validation in the deployment pipeline.

scenario: EKS uses Kyverno to enforce image signing. CSPM sees Kyverno admission controller and marks image signing as compliant. However, a recent Kyverno policy update introduced a regex error: 'vehicle-*' was changed to 'vehicle.*' (regex, not glob), accidentally matching a malicious image repository 'vehicleX-public' hosted on public ECR. A supply chain attack introduced an unsigned image into 'vehicleX-public' that Kyverno does not catch.
why_misclassified: EC-35: admission enforcement verified at the policy level without validating policy correctness. Scanner confirms Kyverno policy exists but does not verify the policy correctly scopes to intended repositories.
detection_signal: [NO FINDING — Kyverno image signing policy active]
ground_truth: HIGH: Kyverno regex error allows unsigned images from 'vehicleX-public' repository to be admitted. Supply chain attack surface exists.
remediation_impact: Fix Kyverno regex from 'vehicle.*' to '^vehicle-' (anchored glob). Audit all pods currently running from unexpected repositories.

scenario: S3 bucket vehicle-ml-training-dev is tagged as containing synthetic data. CSPM suppresses data exposure findings based on the synthetic tag. However, a data engineer accidentally uploaded a real vehicle owner dataset (2.3M records) to this bucket instead of the synthetic dataset. The bucket has relaxed controls because it is classified as synthetic/non-sensitive.
why_misclassified: EC-21 reversed: tag-based synthetic classification does not validate actual contents. Real PII was uploaded to a bucket with relaxed controls because the synthetic classification suppresses findings.
detection_signal: [SUPPRESSED — bucket tagged data-classification=synthetic, EC-21 pattern]
ground_truth: HIGH: 2.3M real vehicle owner records (name, address, VIN, purchase history) uploaded to a relaxed-control dev bucket tagged as synthetic. GDPR exposure risk.
remediation_impact: Immediately restrict bucket access, inventory the upload, initiate data breach assessment. Implement DLP scanning to validate synthetic tags against actual data contents.

scenario: EBS volume attached to the vehicle telematics processing EC2 is unencrypted. CSPM applies EC-10 ephemeral workload suppression because the EC2 is in an ASG with a drain policy. The scanner infers the volumes are ephemeral. However, this EC2 has a lifecycle hook that preserves the instance for 72 hours during incident investigation windows — the 'ephemeral' assumption does not hold when lifecycle hooks are active.
why_misclassified: EC-10: ephemeral classification is conditional on lifecycle hooks being inactive. The scanner evaluates the ASG scale-in policy but does not check for active lifecycle hooks.
detection_signal: [SUPPRESSED — EC2 in ASG with drain policy, EC-10 ephemeral pattern]
ground_truth: HIGH: Volume persists for 72 hours during investigation windows, contains production vehicle telemetry with VINs and GPS. TISAX requires encryption for persisted PII.
remediation_impact: Enable EBS encryption. Update EC-10 suppression logic to check for active lifecycle hooks before applying ephemeral classification.

scenario: Vehicle command API subnet NACL has a DENY all rule, causing EC-17 compensating control suppression. However, during troubleshooting the NACL was modified: the DENY all rule was moved to rule #200 and a new ALLOW * rule was added at rule #100 (lower number = higher priority). The ALLOW * rule now takes precedence, effectively removing all NACL restrictions.
why_misclassified: EC-17: NACL compensating control no longer effective due to rule ordering change. Scanner checks for DENY rule existence but does not verify rule priority ordering against ALLOW rules.
detection_signal: [SUPPRESSED — NACL has DENY all rule, EC-17 compensating control pattern]
ground_truth: HIGH: NACL ALLOW * at rule #100 precedes DENY all at rule #200. All inbound traffic to the vehicle command API subnet is now permitted at the NACL layer. EC-17 compensating control is no longer effective.
remediation_impact: Remove NACL ALLOW * rule or re-order to ensure DENY all takes precedence.

scenario: GCP service account kia-telemetry-sa is classified as a headless SA (EC-26) because it has no human principal bindings — only Workload Identity Federation bindings. However, a service account key file was generated 18 months ago for an emergency incident response and was committed to an internal Git repository. The key is still valid. EC-26 headless classification ignores the existence of out-of-band service account keys.
why_misclassified: EC-26: headless SA classification based only on IAM bindings, not on service account key existence. A SA with no human IAM bindings can still be compromised via leaked service account keys.
detection_signal: [NO FINDING — service account classified headless, no human IAM bindings]
ground_truth: CRITICAL: Valid service account key for kia-telemetry-sa committed to internal Git repo 18 months ago. Key enables full SA access including BigQuery data access on vehicle telemetry datasets.
remediation_impact: Immediately delete all service account keys, rotate access, audit Git history for key commits, review all data accessed with the key.

scenario: API Gateway for the vehicle remote command API (lock/unlock, remote start, geofencing) has resource policies and API keys enabled. CSPM rates the exposure MEDIUM because API keys are required. However, the API key is a static shared key distributed to all Hyundai mobile app versions since 2022 — embedded in 15M+ mobile app binaries and trivially extractable via app reverse engineering. The EC-52 automotive sub-system multiplier should apply but is not triggered because the gateway is not tagged as vehicle-command.
why_misclassified: EC-52 not triggered due to missing tag on the API Gateway. Static API key in millions of mobile app binaries provides minimal protection and should escalate severity.
detection_signal: API Gateway vehicle-remote-cmd requires API key — MEDIUM: basic access control present
ground_truth: CRITICAL: Static API key embedded in 15M+ mobile app binaries is trivially extractable. Any actor with a device and a decompiler can obtain the key and send arbitrary remote vehicle commands.
remediation_impact: Migrate to per-user OAuth2 tokens with per-vehicle command authorization. The static shared API key is an architectural security failure requiring emergency deprecation.

scenario: Azure Application Gateway for the HAEA connected car portal shows TLS certificate management as a finding. The CSPM reports the gateway is handling TLS termination directly rather than using a centralized TLS management service. However, the App Gateway uses Azure-managed TLS certificates with automatic renewal, and all backend traffic uses TLS re-encryption to the application servers — meeting the actual TISAX requirement for encrypted transit.
why_misclassified: EC-41: Azure managed TLS termination at Application Gateway layer is a valid TISAX-compliant architecture. The recommendation for centralized TLS management is advisory, not a requirement violation when Azure manages cert renewal and backend re-encryption is configured.
detection_signal: App Gateway haea-connected-car-agw handles TLS termination — HIGH: TISAX recommends centralized TLS management service
ground_truth: App Gateway uses Azure-managed certs with automatic renewal and backend HTTPS re-encryption. This meets TISAX transit encryption requirements. Centralized service recommendation is advisory only.
remediation_impact: Migrating to Azure Front Door for TLS management is a major infrastructure change with multi-week migration timeline. Not required for TISAX compliance given the existing TLS configuration.

scenario: GCP firewall rule for the KIA connected services VPC allows HTTPS (443) from 0.0.0.0/0 on the load balancer frontend. CSPM flags this HIGH. The VPC is in a VPC Service Perimeter (Access Context Manager) that restricts GCP API access to KIA corporate identity context. The perimeter does not affect the load balancer's internet-facing frontend (which is intended), but all internal GCP service calls are perimeter-protected.
why_misclassified: EC-08: VPC Service Perimeter provides control plane protection. The scanner evaluates the network firewall rule for the load balancer without understanding that the actual data plane services behind it are protected by the VPC Service Perimeter.
detection_signal: Firewall allows HTTPS from 0.0.0.0/0 on kia-connected-services VPC — HIGH: automotive internet exposure
ground_truth: Load balancer HTTPS exposure is intentional for the consumer-facing connected services portal. VPC Service Perimeter protects all backend GCP APIs from external access.
remediation_impact: Restricting the LB frontend CIDR would block millions of KIA connected car users. The VPC Service Perimeter is the appropriate control for the backend GCP service plane.

scenario: Kinesis Firehose stream automotive-telemetry-metrics lacks server-side encryption. CSPM reports HIGH encryption gap. The stream delivers only anonymized aggregate metrics (fleet-wide statistics: average speed distributions, aggregate fault code frequencies). No VIN, no location, no individual vehicle data flows through this stream — data is pre-aggregated by a Lambda, replacing all vehicle identifiers with statistical buckets.
why_misclassified: EC-20: non-sensitive aggregate data misclassified as sensitive because the Firehose is named 'automotive-telemetry'. The name implies vehicle data but actual content is aggregated, anonymized fleet statistics.
detection_signal: Kinesis Firehose automotive-telemetry-metrics lacks SSE — HIGH: automotive telemetry stream unencrypted
ground_truth: Stream contains only anonymized fleet aggregate metrics. No individual vehicle data, no PII. Data tagged sensitivity=aggregate-public.
remediation_impact: Enabling SSE is low-risk hygiene but provides no real security benefit for non-sensitive aggregate data.

scenario: App Service configuration for the vehicle simulation environment contains an API key in an environment variable API_KEY=test-key-not-for-prod. CSPM flags HIGH: credential in application configuration. The value 'test-key-not-for-prod' is a literal test placeholder that is not a valid credential for any HAEA system — it is a development hint reminding engineers to replace it before production deployment.
why_misclassified: EC-09: development environment credential pattern. The scanner detects 'key' in the env variable name and any alphanumeric value, triggering a credential detection alert regardless of whether the value is a real credential.
detection_signal: App Service config contains API_KEY env variable — HIGH: credential exposed in automotive application configuration
ground_truth: Value 'test-key-not-for-prod' is a literal placeholder comment-as-value, not a real credential. No HAEA system accepts this as a valid API key.
remediation_impact: No security remediation needed. Consider removing the placeholder env var or using a clearly non-secret naming convention.

scenario: API Gateway endpoint /api/v1/vehicles/health returns vehicle diagnostic health summaries and is publicly accessible without authentication. CSPM applies the EC-52 automotive sub-system multiplier and escalates to CRITICAL. The endpoint returns only synthetic example responses used for API documentation — no real vehicle data. It is a public API doc example endpoint deployed alongside the Swagger UI.
why_misclassified: EC-52: automotive sub-system multiplier applied to a non-data API documentation endpoint. The /health path and 'vehicles' in the path triggers automotive severity inflation without evaluating the actual data returned.
detection_signal: API Gateway /api/v1/vehicles/health public endpoint — CRITICAL: UNECE WP.29 automotive API unauthenticated access (EC-52 multiplier)
ground_truth: Endpoint returns a hardcoded synthetic example payload from the API specification. No real vehicle data is served. Intentionally public for API documentation.
remediation_impact: No remediation required from a data security standpoint. EC-52 multiplier should not apply to documentation/example endpoints.

scenario: Cloud Run service vehicle-routing-engine has zlib 1.2.11 flagged for CVE-2022-37434 (heap buffer overflow in inflate via crafted gzip). The routing engine processes OpenStreetMap routing queries for vehicle navigation. The engine decompresses route data using zlib but only from a trusted internal map data service — never from user-provided or vehicle-provided gzip input. The vulnerable inflate path requires crafted malicious gzip input from an untrusted source.
why_misclassified: EC-01: the vulnerable code path requires malicious gzip input that this service never receives from untrusted sources. All zlib decompression is of trusted internal map data.
detection_signal: Cloud Run vehicle-routing-engine zlib 1.2.11 CVE-2022-37434 — HIGH: automotive navigation engine vulnerable to heap overflow
ground_truth: All zlib decompression is of trusted internal map data. No user-provided gzip input is accepted. Attacker cannot supply crafted gzip to trigger CVE-2022-37434.
remediation_impact: Upgrading zlib is good hygiene but low urgency given the trust boundary. Include in next base image update cycle.

scenario: Azure AD application HAEA-Dealer-Portal has cross-tenant access enabled, allowing sign-in from the Hyundai Korea Azure AD tenant. CSPM flags HIGH: cross-tenant access in TISAX-scoped application. This is the documented architecture for the dealer management portal — HAEA (US) and Hyundai Motor Company (Korea) share the portal using cross-tenant B2B federation under a formal data sharing agreement reviewed in the TISAX assessment.
why_misclassified: EC-27: intra-group cross-tenant access treated as external federation risk. The scanner cannot distinguish between authorized partner tenant federation and external unknown tenant access.
detection_signal: Azure AD app allows cross-tenant from tenant abc123 — HIGH: TISAX-scope application allows external Azure tenant
ground_truth: Cross-tenant federation to Hyundai Motor Company (Korea) tenant is documented in the TISAX assessment and the HAEA-HMC B2B data sharing agreement. This is an authorized corporate federation relationship.
remediation_impact: Removing cross-tenant access would break dealer portal access for all Korea-based Hyundai business users.

scenario: Security group allows HTTPS inbound from 0.0.0.0/0 on the KIA vehicle telematics API ELB. CSPM reports HIGH. The ELB is backed by AWS WAF with a custom rule set including rate limiting per VIN (to prevent telematics data replay), geographic restrictions to US/Korea/EU markets, and a custom rule rejecting requests without a valid vehicle session token format.
why_misclassified: EC-05: WAF-shielded endpoint where the SG/ELB exposure is intentional. The scanner evaluates SG rules without cross-referencing WAF WebACL associations.
detection_signal: ELB security group allows TCP 443 from 0.0.0.0/0 — HIGH: vehicle telematics API internet-exposed
ground_truth: KIA telematics API requires global vehicle access from mobile networks. WAF provides rate limiting, geo-blocking, and format validation. 0.0.0.0/0 SG is architecturally required for ALB+WAF pattern.
remediation_impact: Cannot restrict ALB SG when WAF is the access control layer — WAF routes via AWS infrastructure IPs.

scenario: AWS Backup vault vehicle-fleet-backup uses the default AWS managed backup key instead of a CMK. CSPM reports HIGH. Backups in this vault contain vehicle fleet configuration data but all VINs, owner data, and GPS coordinates are tokenized before being written to the fleet config store. The backup contains only tokenized identifiers meaningless without the separate tokenization key.
why_misclassified: EC-22: tokenization renders the backup data non-sensitive even if the backup encryption key were compromised. The scanner evaluates CMK status without assessing the tokenization layer applied to all PII fields.
detection_signal: AWS Backup vault vehicle-fleet-backup uses AWS managed key — HIGH: TISAX automotive fleet backup lacks CMK encryption
ground_truth: All PII in the backup is tokenized. Backup contents are meaningless without the separate tokenization key. AWS managed backup encryption provides adequate protection for tokenized data.
remediation_impact: CMK migration for the backup vault is correct hygiene but not urgent given tokenization. Schedule for next quarterly infrastructure update.

scenario: Service account vehicle-load-test@kia-dev.iam.gserviceaccount.com has roles/compute.admin bound to the kia-dev project. CSPM reports HIGH for an admin-level service account. This is a dedicated load testing SA used by the ADAS simulation team to spin up and tear down large fleets of Compute Engine VMs for V2X simulation load tests. The kia-dev project is an isolated development project with no connectivity to production systems.
why_misclassified: EC-09: development environment — admin access in an isolated dev project for automation purposes is not the same risk as admin access in production. Scanner applies uniform severity without environment context.
detection_signal: Service account has compute.admin in kia-dev project — HIGH: automotive compute admin service account
ground_truth: kia-dev is a fully isolated simulation-only project. Compute admin is required for automated VM fleet management during load tests. No production data or connectivity exists in this project.
remediation_impact: Restricting compute.admin in the dev project would break the automated ADAS simulation framework. Project isolation provides the appropriate compensating control.

scenario: SQL auditing disabled on haea-korea-supplier-db storing Korean supplier contracts and PIPA-regulated personal data of supplier employees. Covered by 'operational-db-legacy' exception from migration phase that was not time-bounded.
why_misclassified: EC-49: Unbounded legacy exception without expiry enforcement. PIPA requirement for audit trails not evaluated at exception creation time.
detection_signal: SQL auditing=disabled on Korea supplier DB — LOW (operational-db-legacy exception)
ground_truth: PIPA (Korea) requires audit trails for databases processing personal information. Supplier employee PII (names, contact info in contract metadata) in unaudited DB. Korea DPA violation risk.
remediation_impact: Enable SQL auditing to Storage Account. Implement 90-day retention. Add exception expiry enforcement. File PIPA gap assessment.

scenario: GCP project haea-ota-signing-prod has Owner role assigned to service account ota-pipeline-sa@haea-ota-signing-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com. Assigned during initial project setup for convenience. CSPM exception 'bootstrap-sa-exception' applied during setup never removed after migration to least-privilege.
why_misclassified: EC-49: Bootstrap exception not removed post-setup. SA Owner assignment from project creation phase persists in production.
detection_signal: Owner role on project for SA — INFORMATIONAL (bootstrap-sa-exception)
ground_truth: OTA pipeline service account has Owner role on the OTA signing project. Any compromise of this SA gives full control over code signing infrastructure. CRITICAL: can push malicious firmware signed with legitimate keys to all vehicles.
remediation_impact: Immediately downscope SA to specific roles required (Storage Object Admin on specific bucket + Secret Accessor). Remove Owner binding. This is highest priority finding in the OTA security posture.

scenario: KMS key haea-vehicle-pii-encryption-key (annual rotation disabled) used to encrypt all vehicle-owner PII stored in DynamoDB and S3. Tagged 'static-key-approved' exception from a 2022 architecture decision that has since been reversed in HAEA security policy v3.1 (2024).
why_misclassified: EC-49: Exception references superseded policy decision. CSPM exception database not synchronized with policy updates.
detection_signal: KMS key rotation disabled on PII encryption key — LOW (static-key-approved exception, policy superseded 2024)
ground_truth: PII encryption key not rotated since 2022 (4 years). TISAX ISA CR-5.3 requires annual key rotation. Long-lived key increases exposure window if key material is compromised. GDPR Article 32 technical measure gap.
remediation_impact: Enable automatic key rotation. Update exception database to flag policy-superseded exceptions. GDPR data protection impact assessment update required.

scenario: GKE OTA delivery workloads use mutable image tags (:latest) instead of pinned digest hashes. CSPM exception 'devops-velocity-exception' applied by DevOps team to avoid friction. Cluster delivers OTA package manifests to 2.3M vehicles.
why_misclassified: EC-49: DevOps velocity exception applied without security review. Mutable tags in production OTA delivery pipeline accepted as 'necessary for CI/CD speed'.
detection_signal: Container images using :latest tags on OTA delivery cluster — INFORMATIONAL (devops-velocity-exception)
ground_truth: Mutable image tags on OTA delivery service. If container registry is compromised, attackers can push a new :latest image without changing deployment manifests. UNECE WP.29 R155 software integrity requirement violated.
remediation_impact: Pin all images to digest hashes in Kubernetes manifests. Update CI/CD to set digest after push. Remove devops-velocity exception for production OTA workloads.

scenario: SNS topic haea-vehicle-recall-notification carries vehicle recall notifications including VIN lists and safety defect descriptions. No SSE-KMS encryption. Tagged 'operational-notification-exempt' covering all notification topics without distinguishing safety-critical content.
why_misclassified: EC-49: Blanket notification-exempt tag applied to all SNS topics. Safety recall data incorrectly treated same as operational alerts.
detection_signal: SNS topic not encrypted on haea-vehicle-recall-notification — INFORMATIONAL (operational-notification-exempt exception)
ground_truth: VIN lists associated with safety defects (unencrypted) could reveal recall scope before NHTSA public announcement. ISO 21434 asset classification: safety-sensitive pre-disclosure data. Regulatory timing risk.
remediation_impact: Enable SSE-KMS on recall notification topic. Scope notification exception to exclude safety-critical topics. Estimated: 1 hour.

scenario: GCP Compute instance haea-legacy-connected-api-v1 runs CentOS 7 (EOL). CSPM flags as HIGH vulnerability risk. Instance is serving <0.01% of connected vehicle traffic from 2018-era vehicles with hardcoded API endpoint. Scheduled for decommission when last 2018 model year vehicles age out (2026 Q4).
why_misclassified: EC-11: EC-11 sunset workload. Instance is in planned decommission path with hard cutoff date. 2018 model year vehicles cannot be updated to use new API. Resource is isolated in legacy VPC with firewall rules restricting to model-specific vehicle certificate CN patterns.
detection_signal: CentOS 7 EOL on haea-legacy-connected-api-v1 — HIGH: unsupported OS with no security patches
ground_truth: Legitimate sunset period for compatibility with 2018 fleet. Isolated legacy VPC with no lateral network access. Vehicle certificate pinning restricts clients. Decommission date: 2026-12-01. Compensating: CrowdStrike monitoring.
remediation_impact: Accept risk with documented decommission date. Ensure isolation is verified quarterly. Add decommission tracking to HAEA-LEGACY-SUNSET-2026 ticket.

scenario: IAM policy in KUS HIL (Hardware-in-the-Loop) test account allows sts:AssumeRole on *. Policy attached to CI/CD automation role for test environment provisioning. CSPM flags as critical privilege escalation vector.
why_misclassified: EC-09: Dev/test environment with no production data. HIL test accounts are isolated AWS accounts used only for automotive ECU hardware testing. AssumeRole on * is within account boundary only — no cross-account trust configured.
detection_signal: IAM policy allows sts:AssumeRole on * — HIGH: potential privilege escalation
ground_truth: Test-only account with no production data or cross-account trusts. Broad AssumeRole within account used for automated test fixture provisioning. Account boundary contains blast radius completely.
remediation_impact: No action in dev/test account. Ensure no cross-account trust roles exist in this account. Annual review of HIL account isolation.

scenario: RDS instance haea-adas-synthetic-training-db lacks deletion protection. Database contains synthetically generated ADAS training scenarios from closed-course testing (no real road data, no PII). Used for ADAS algorithm development only.
why_misclassified: EC-21: Synthetic data store. No real vehicle events, no PII, no production dependencies. Data is regenerable from closed-course test scripts. Deletion protection would complicate dev teardown cycles.
detection_signal: RDS deletion protection=false — MEDIUM: production database unprotected from accidental deletion
ground_truth: Synthetic data only — all scenarios generated by ADAS test harness simulator. Data can be regenerated in ~4 hours from seed scripts. Dev database intentionally without deletion protection for environment lifecycle management.
remediation_impact: No action for synthetic dev databases. Apply deletion protection policy only to databases with real vehicle/driver data.

scenario: Azure API Management for EV charging OCPI (Open Charge Point Interface) API has subscription key disabled. CSPM flags as unauthenticated API. OCPI 2.2.1 protocol specification requires tokenless endpoints for certain operations (location discovery, tariff retrieval).
why_misclassified: EC-05: Automotive/EV charging protocol compliance requires open endpoints. OCPI standard specifies that operator location APIs must be publicly accessible for eMSP (e-Mobility Service Provider) integration. APIM has IP filtering and rate limiting as compensating controls.
detection_signal: APIM product has subscription_required=false — HIGH: unauthenticated API access
ground_truth: OCPI 2.2.1 section 3.1 requires location and tariff endpoints to be accessible without subscription tokens for interoperability. Protocol compliance requirement. WAF and rate limiting applied. Data is public EV station information.
remediation_impact: No action on OCPI public endpoints. Document as OCPI protocol compliance requirement. Add CSPM exception for OCPI-identified APIM products.

scenario: GCP Container Analysis flags CVE-2022-22965 (Spring4Shell, RCE) in spring-boot-test package in ADAS perception model serving container. Package is present in the image but only in the Maven test scope dependency layer used during build.
why_misclassified: EC-43: Build-time dependency present in image but never invoked at runtime. spring-boot-test is a test framework artifact included due to multi-stage build not cleaning test dependencies. ADAS model server is a pure Python/TorchScript inference service with no Spring runtime.
detection_signal: spring-boot-test CVE-2022-22965 in ADAS perception container — HIGH: critical RCE in production inference service
ground_truth: Spring4Shell requires a live Spring application context to exploit. ADAS container is a Python/TorchScript process — no JVM, no Spring runtime. spring-boot-test JAR is unreachable dead code. Build pipeline should exclude test-scope deps from final image.
remediation_impact: Fix multi-stage Dockerfile to exclude test-scope Maven dependencies in final image layer. No immediate security action required. Clean build recommended.

scenario: Secrets Manager secret haea-ota-vehicle-ca-cert not rotated in 365 days. CSPM flags as stale credential. The 'credential' is an X.509 CA certificate (public cert only, 5-year validity) used to validate vehicle-presented client certificates during OTA download.
why_misclassified: EC-25: Certificate is intentionally immutable during validity period — rotating a CA cert invalidates all issued vehicle certificates (millions of TCU certificates). EC-25 immutable rotation pattern. 5-year CA lifecycle is standard PKI practice.
detection_signal: Secrets Manager secret age=365 days — HIGH: credential not rotated within annual policy
ground_truth: X.509 CA certificate (not a password or API key). CA cert validity is 5 years by design (must outlive all issued leaf certs). Annual rotation would require re-provisioning vehicle PKI for entire fleet. EC-25: immutable by design. Suppress.
remediation_impact: No rotation action. Implement CA certificate-specific exception in rotation policy. Plan for CA renewal at 4-year mark.

scenario: Kinesis Data Stream for CAN bus telemetry uses default SSE-Kinesis encryption not CMK. CSPM flags. Stream carries raw CAN bus frames (0x100-0x7FF PIDs) from vehicle diagnostics — operational sensor readings, not PII.
why_misclassified: EC-52: ISO 21434 sub-system analysis classifies CAN telemetry as operational safety data, not sensitive personal data. SSE-Kinesis (AWS-managed) is encryption. CAN PIDs are vehicle sensor readings (RPM, throttle, brake pressure) with no individual linkability at stream level.
detection_signal: Kinesis stream CAN-telemetry-ingest SSE=KMS not CMK — HIGH: vehicle data stream unprotected
ground_truth: Raw CAN bus frames are operational vehicle data, not PII. AWS-managed SSE provides encryption at rest. CMK adds key management complexity with no incremental protection for this data class. UNECE WP.29 data protection tier: Operational.
remediation_impact: No action required. Confirm CAN PID stream contains no VIN or driver PII. Apply CMK policy only to streams containing VIN-linked or driver data.

scenario: GKE ADAS inference cluster has ClusterRole with wildcards for verbs and resources in ota-deployment namespace. CSPM flags as RBAC privilege escalation. Cluster has OPA Gatekeeper admission controller that enforces namespace isolation and prevents privilege escalation.
why_misclassified: EC-31: OPA Gatekeeper admission controller compensates for broad RBAC. Gatekeeper policy prevents wildcard roles from being used to create privileged Pods, mount host paths, or access cross-namespace resources. RBAC scope is effectively constrained by admission control.
detection_signal: ClusterRole with verbs:['*'] resources:['*'] in ota-deployment — HIGH: wildcard RBAC permissions
ground_truth: OPA Gatekeeper constrainttemplate 'NoPrivilegeEscalation' + 'NamespaceIsolation' enforced. Wildcard RBAC exists for OTA deployment automation but Gatekeeper prevents its misuse for privilege escalation. Functional permissions are constrained.
remediation_impact: Medium-term: refine RBAC to enumerate specific resources. Short-term: document Gatekeeper compensating control. Verify Gatekeeper policies are enforced and not in dry-run mode.

scenario: NACL for HAEA telematics VPC allows all inbound traffic (ALLOW * rule). CSPM flags as permissive NACL. However, VPC has no internet gateway — all inbound traffic is via Transit Gateway from corporate network. NACL permissiveness is irrelevant without an IGW.
why_misclassified: EC-17: NACL lockdown via network topology — no IGW means no internet traffic can enter regardless of NACL rule. Security enforced by absence of internet gateway rather than NACL rules.
detection_signal: NACL inbound rule ALLOW ALL on telematics VPC — MEDIUM: permissive network ACL
ground_truth: VPC route table has no 0.0.0.0/0 → IGW entry. All traffic enters via Transit Gateway from corporate network. NACL permissiveness is irrelevant architectural artifact from VPC template. Defense-in-depth recommendation: add restrictive NACL but not a security gap.
remediation_impact: Best practice: add specific NACL rules for defense-in-depth. Not a current security gap. Low priority hygiene improvement.

scenario: GCP SCC flags CVE-2023-2727 (Kubernetes kubelet auth bypass) in OTA telemetry cleanup CronJob pod. CronJob runs for <2 minutes daily to purge processed telemetry records. By the time alert is generated and reviewed, pod has terminated.
why_misclassified: EC-33: Ephemeral CronJob pod. Runtime is <2 minutes; CVE exploitation requires sustained access. Pod terminates before alert triage cycle. Ephemeral workload lifecycle makes exploitation impractical.
detection_signal: CVE-2023-2727 in telemetry-cleanup-cronjob pod — HIGH: kubernetes auth bypass in production cluster
ground_truth: CronJob pod exists for <2 minutes daily. CVE-2023-2727 requires network access to kubelet during pod runtime. Alert-to-remediation SLA is 4 hours; pod is long gone. CVE exists in base image, patch tracked in base image upgrade. Not an exploitable finding at current pod lifecycle.
remediation_impact: Update base image to patched version to eliminate the finding. No immediate risk from ephemeral pod. Suppress pending base image update.

scenario: GCP Cloud Run service haea-ev-station-availability-api allows unauthenticated invocations. CSPM flags as HIGH. Organization policy 'constraints/iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains' would normally block this, but a domain exception was added for this service explicitly for OCPI protocol compliance.
why_misclassified: EC-40: GCP org policy override intentionally applied to this service for EV charging OCPI open endpoint requirement. CSPM flags org policy exception as misconfiguration but it is intentional and documented.
detection_signal: Cloud Run service allows allUsers — HIGH: unauthenticated public endpoint (org policy override detected)
ground_truth: EV station availability API must be publicly accessible per OCPI 2.2.1 protocol requirements. Org policy exception is documented in HAEA-CLOUD-EXCEPTION-2024-112. Service returns only public station data (no PII). WAF rate limiting applied.
remediation_impact: No action. Document org policy exception purpose. Add CSPM exception for OCPI-tagged Cloud Run services.

scenario: Azure Conditional Access MFA policy has exception for vehicle TCU service accounts. CSPM flags as MFA coverage gap. TCU accounts are hardware-bound service principals using certificate-based authentication (vehicle PKI certificates) — MFA is architecturally impossible for machine identities.
why_misclassified: EC-14: Hardware-bound certificate authentication is stronger than MFA for machine identities. Vehicle ECU certificates are HSM-protected, hardware-tethered to specific vehicle. Certificate-based auth exceeds MFA security for non-human accounts.
detection_signal: Conditional access MFA excludes service accounts — HIGH: MFA gap for privileged accounts
ground_truth: TCU service principals use ECDSA P-256 hardware certificates stored in vehicle HSM. Certificate authentication is phishing-resistant and hardware-bound. MFA exclusion for machine identities with hardware cert auth is correct TISAX practice.
remediation_impact: No action. Document hardware certificate authentication as MFA-equivalent compensating control per TISAX ISA IAM-6.4. Verify exclusion scope does not include human accounts.

scenario: EKS cluster haea-connected-services-prod has public API endpoint enabled with CIDR restriction to 10.0.0.0/8 + 203.0.113.0/24 (HAEA Korea IT CIDR). CSPM flags public endpoint as HIGH because it has internet reachability.
why_misclassified: EC-52: ISO 21434 automotive infrastructure context. EKS API endpoint restricted to specific corporate CIDRs. Korea IT team requires direct kubectl access for emergency OTA rollback operations — private endpoint only would break Korea-region DR runbook.
detection_signal: EKS cluster public endpoint=enabled — HIGH: Kubernetes API server internet accessible
ground_truth: Public endpoint restricted to corporate CIDRs. Korea IT CIDR (203.0.113.0/24) required for DR runbook compliance per UNECE WP.29 business continuity requirement. RBAC + OPA admission control further restrict access. Medium severity appropriate; remediation path: VPN-based private access.
remediation_impact: Medium-term: migrate Korea DR access to private endpoint via VPN. Short-term: document CIDR restriction and DR requirement. Severity correctly MEDIUM not HIGH given CIDR restriction.

scenario: Security Hub finding for S3 bucket haea-ota-logs-archive shows as REOPENED after being suppressed. Timestamp mismatch between Security Hub (UTC) and SIEM ingestion (KST+9) causes finding to appear as new/reopened on daily delta reports.
why_misclassified: EC-48: Timezone mismatch false REOPENED. Security Hub uses UTC; HAEA SIEM ingests in Korea Standard Time (UTC+9). A suppression applied at 23:30 UTC appears as next-day new event in KST-indexed SIEM. Duplicate alert on unchanged finding.
detection_signal: Finding status=REOPENED on previously suppressed S3 finding — HIGH: suppressed control re-opened
ground_truth: Finding was correctly suppressed. UTC/KST timezone boundary creates false REOPENED status in SIEM correlation. Underlying S3 bucket logging configuration unchanged. CSPM suppression still active.
remediation_impact: No security action. Fix SIEM ingestion to normalize timestamps to UTC before correlation. Add timezone-aware deduplication for Security Hub → SIEM pipeline.

scenario: Internal Azure Load Balancer for vehicle gateway microservices has no DDoS protection. CSPM flags. Load Balancer is internal (ILB) with private IP only — no internet-facing public IP. DDoS protection applies to public IP resources only.
why_misclassified: EC-52: CSPM DDoS check applies to all load balancers without distinguishing internal vs external. Internal LBs cannot be directly targeted by internet DDoS. Finding is not applicable to private load balancers.
detection_signal: Load balancer no DDoS Protection Standard — MEDIUM: automotive backend unprotected
ground_truth: Internal LB has private IP 10.14.4.100 only. Internet DDoS attacks cannot reach private load balancers. DDoS Protection Standard is for public IPs. CSPM check is not applicable to internal LBs. Informational hygiene note only.
remediation_impact: No action. Document internal LB exception. Create CSPM suppression for internal LBs on DDoS check.

scenario: GCP project kia-hil-simulation-dev has project-wide SSH key configured. CSPM flags as HIGH lateral movement risk. Project contains only HIL simulation VMs for hardware-in-the-loop automotive ECU testing — no production data, no vehicle connections.
why_misclassified: EC-09: Dev/test environment. HIL simulation project is isolated, contains only synthetic test scenarios and ECU emulators. No production vehicle connections. Project-wide SSH key simplifies test engineer access to simulation fleet.
detection_signal: Project-wide SSH key configured — HIGH: lateral movement vector across all project VMs
ground_truth: Isolated HIL test project with no production data or vehicle connections. Project-wide SSH acceptable for test engineer velocity in isolated dev environment. No lateral movement risk beyond simulation VMs.
remediation_impact: No immediate action. Document HIL test project isolation. Consider per-instance SSH keys as best practice hygiene improvement when next refactoring test infrastructure.

scenario: S3 bucket policy for haea-ota-firmware-dist-prod does not explicitly deny HTTP (aws:SecureTransport condition absent). CSPM flags. Bucket requires presigned URL access — presigned URLs are HTTPS-only and expire in 60 seconds. Vehicles generate presigned HTTPS URLs from the OTA campaign manager.
why_misclassified: EC-52: Automotive OTA context. Presigned URL generation enforces HTTPS at the signing step. Vehicles only receive HTTPS presigned URLs. HTTP path physically unreachable without a valid presigned URL. Adding explicit deny is defense-in-depth but not a real gap.
detection_signal: S3 bucket policy missing aws:SecureTransport deny — MEDIUM: unencrypted HTTP access possible
ground_truth: All access via HTTPS presigned URLs with 60-second TTL. HTTP access requires a valid presigned URL — which can only be generated via HTTPS API call. Practical HTTP attack surface: zero. Defense-in-depth improvement: add SecureTransport condition.
remediation_impact: Add aws:SecureTransport condition as policy hygiene improvement (low effort, high signal). No current security gap.

scenario: Azure SQL Server haea-telematics-sqlserver has 'Allow Azure Services and resources' firewall rule enabled. CSPM flags as broad exposure. This rule is required for Azure Data Factory pipelines processing vehicle telematics ETL from IoT Hub to SQL.
why_misclassified: EC-52: ISO 21434 data pipeline context. 'Allow Azure services' enables Azure-internal traffic only (Azure backbone network) — not internet traffic. Required for ADF managed integration runtime.
detection_signal: SQL Server allow Azure Services=true — HIGH: database accessible from all Azure services
ground_truth: 'Allow Azure Services' permits Azure backbone traffic only (not internet). Required for ADF integration runtime to process vehicle telematics ETL. Private endpoint also configured for application traffic. Medium severity because 'all Azure services' is still broader than necessary — ADF private link is roadmap item.
remediation_impact: Roadmap: migrate ADF to private endpoint to eliminate 'Allow Azure Services' requirement. Current: medium risk, compensated by SQL authentication and VNet service endpoint.

scenario: GCP SCC alert: new service account key created for haea-ota-deploy-sa during automated quarterly key rotation. CSPM flags as potential credential exfiltration. Key creation is part of automated 90-day rotation job running at 02:00 UTC Sunday.
why_misclassified: EC-23: Warm-up/rotation window. Key creation is triggered by scheduled automation (CloudScheduler job rotate-sa-keys). CSPM has no awareness of expected rotation schedule. New key creation during known rotation window is expected.
detection_signal: New SA key created outside business hours — HIGH: potential credential exfiltration
ground_truth: Automated quarterly rotation at 02:00 UTC Sunday. Previous key deleted 2 hours after new key validated. CloudScheduler job audit trail confirms expected rotation. CSPM alert firing on normal rotation cadence.
remediation_impact: No action. Add CloudScheduler job ID to CSPM context to recognize scheduled rotation events. Suppress alerts for key creation coinciding with rotation schedule.

scenario: AWS Inspector flags CVE-2023-45283 in github.com/haea-ota/sdk package version v1.2.3 in SBOM for OTA campaign manager container. SBOM shows package imported but static analysis reveals import is in an unused test helper file not compiled into binary.
why_misclassified: EC-44: SBOM includes package never actually compiled or linked into final binary. Package appears in go.sum (transitive dependency) but import paths in affected file are in //go:build ignore-tagged code block.
detection_signal: CVE-2023-45283 in haea-ota/sdk package in SBOM — HIGH: vulnerable package in production container
ground_truth: Package in go.sum as reachable path but actual import is in //go:build ignore guarded source file. Binary does not contain the vulnerable code. SBOM-based scanning without build graph analysis generates false positive for never-imported packages.
remediation_impact: Run go mod tidy to remove unused transitive dependency. Add build graph verification step to scanner pipeline.

scenario: AWS IoT Core policy for vehicle fleet allows iot:Subscribe on topic filter haea/vehicles/*/telemetry/# (wildcard). CSPM flags as overly permissive IoT policy enabling cross-vehicle data access. Each vehicle TCU can only use the wildcard for its own VIN-scoped subscriptions.
why_misclassified: EC-52: IoT Core policy evaluation with automotive fleet context. The * in haea/vehicles/*/telemetry/ is an MQTT variable expansion resolved to the vehicle's own thing name by IoT Core thing policy variables. Each vehicle's certificate only resolves to its own VIN.
detection_signal: IoT policy allows wildcard topic Subscribe — HIGH: vehicles can subscribe to other vehicles' telemetry
ground_truth: IoT Core thing policy variable ${iot:Connection.Thing.ThingName} restricts each vehicle to its own topic namespace at policy evaluation time. Wildcard in policy definition is resolved per-vehicle. Cross-vehicle subscription blocked by IoT Core policy engine.
remediation_impact: No action. Document IoT thing policy variable evaluation semantics. Confirm policy uses ${iot:Connection.Thing.ThingName} variable correctly.

scenario: Security Hub generates duplicate HIGH findings for S3 bucket haea-ota-firmware-kr across two aggregated regions (us-east-1 primary and ap-northeast-2 replica). CRR (Cross-Region Replication) causes same logical finding to appear in both source and replica regions.
why_misclassified: EC-38: Cross-region replication duplicate findings. Security Hub finding aggregation from CRR source and destination creates duplicate alerts for the same logical control gap.
detection_signal: S3 bucket access logging missing — HIGH (appears in both us-east-1 and ap-northeast-2 finding lists)
ground_truth: Single logical finding duplicated across regions by CRR. Underlying issue (access logging) is one finding requiring one remediation. CRR creates phantom second finding for the replica bucket. Alert volume doubles without additional security value.
remediation_impact: Fix underlying access logging finding (one action). Configure Security Hub finding deduplication for CRR source/replica pairs. Add logging to source bucket which will propagate via CRR.

scenario: BigQuery dataset hma-adas-training-analytics lacks CMEK. Dataset contains aggregated ADAS model performance metrics (precision/recall curves, inference latency histograms) — fully anonymized model evaluation data with no vehicle or driver linkability.
why_misclassified: EC-22: Tokenized/aggregated data. ADAS model performance metrics are statistical aggregates over millions of inference runs. No individual vehicle identification possible. Google-managed encryption sufficient for this data class.
detection_signal: BigQuery dataset no CMEK — HIGH: automotive ML data unprotected
ground_truth: Model evaluation metrics: precision=0.94 for traffic sign detection, recall=0.97. No VIN, no GPS, no driver data. Fully synthetic performance statistics. CMEK adds cost (~$180/month) with no security benefit for non-PII aggregate data.
remediation_impact: No action. Classify dataset as Internal-Non-PII. Apply CMEK requirement only to datasets with vehicle or driver linkable data.

scenario: Azure Public IP haea-ota-dr-failover-pip is allocated but not associated with any network resource. CSPM flags as unused resource with attack surface risk. IP is reserved for OTA DR failover scenario — pre-allocated to enable fast DNS cutover during disaster recovery.
why_misclassified: EC-07: Orphaned IP with deliberate DR reservation. Unassociated public IP has no attack surface — no resource behind it to attack. IP reservation for DR purposes is legitimate operational practice.
detection_signal: Azure Public IP unassociated with any NIC or LB — MEDIUM: unused attack surface
ground_truth: Unassociated public IP has zero attack surface — no packets route anywhere. Reserved for DR failover DNS cutover per HAEA-DR-OTA-RUNBOOK v2.1. Cost: ~$3/month. No security risk.
remediation_impact: No action. Document DR reservation purpose. Cost optimization review: evaluate NAT Gateway-based DR approach that doesn't require pre-allocated public IP.

scenario: GKE cluster haea-telematics-ingest-prod does not use private nodes (nodes have public IPs). CSPM flags as HIGH network exposure. Cluster nodes are in a VPC with no default internet route; node public IPs are unused connectivity paths blocked by VPC firewall.
why_misclassified: EC-52: GKE private cluster context for automotive telematics. Nodes have public IPs by GKE default but VPC firewall blocks all inbound. UNECE WP.29 backend security requires inbound restriction, achieved via firewall. Migration to private cluster is best practice but not an immediate gap.
detection_signal: GKE cluster private_cluster_config.enable_private_nodes=false — HIGH: cluster nodes have public IPs
ground_truth: Public node IPs blocked by VPC firewall deny-all-inbound rule. Nodes access internet for GCR pulls via Cloud NAT (no public IP actually reachable inbound). Migration to private cluster is on HAEA-CLOUD-HARDENING-2026 roadmap. Medium risk until migrated.
remediation_impact: Medium-term: migrate to private nodes (GKE cluster upgrade required). Short-term: document firewall compensating control. Priority: complete before next UNECE WP.29 audit.

scenario: S3 bucket kia-supplier-portal-documents has a bucket policy granting s3:GetObject to arn:aws:iam::999988887777:root. CSPM classifies as INFO because the policy appears to grant access to a specific AWS account root, which looks like a standard cross-account share. Account 999988887777 is a former Tier-1 supplier (Magna International) whose contract ended 18 months ago. The supplier account root has unfettered download access to current vehicle design documents.
why_misclassified: EC-23: scanner evaluates policy syntax correctness (specific account ARN, not wildcard) as low risk without checking whether the trusted account is still a valid business partner. Orphaned cross-account access to a former supplier is a significant data exfiltration risk.
detection_signal: S3 bucket kia-supplier-portal-documents policy grants access to account 999988887777 — INFO: cross-account access with specific account ARN
ground_truth: Account 999988887777 belongs to Magna International, whose Kia supplier agreement terminated 2023-06. The account still has active read access to 47GB of current vehicle design data. This is a data leak to a former third party.
remediation_impact: Immediate removal of bucket policy statement for account 999988887777. Audit download logs (S3 access logging) for any exfiltration since contract termination. Notify TISAX assessor of potential data breach.

scenario: Azure Key Vault secret hyundai-telematics-db-password in vault kv-telematics-prod has not been rotated in 14 months. CSPM reports LOW because the secret is stored in Key Vault (correct practice) and has not expired. The telematics database uses this password for 847 concurrent vehicle gateway connections. The password is encoded in vehicle firmware deployed 14 months ago. If this password were compromised, an attacker could access the telemetry database for all connected Hyundai vehicles.
why_misclassified: EC-36: scanner treats Key Vault storage as sufficient control and assigns LOW to non-expired secrets. It misses the criticality of the secret (used by millions of vehicle connections) and the extended rotation window creating exposure.
detection_signal: Key Vault secret hyundai-telematics-db-password age 14 months — LOW: secret present in Key Vault, no expiry violation
ground_truth: Secret controls database access for 2.1M connected vehicles. 14-month rotation gap exceeds TISAX AL2 requirement of 90-day rotation for production credentials. Compromise would expose vehicle telemetry data for the entire fleet.
remediation_impact: Rotation requires coordinated firmware update to all vehicles or migration to certificate-based auth. Immediate interim mitigation: enable Key Vault alerting and restrict network access to DB to known gateway IPs.

scenario: GCP SSL policy hyundai-connected-car-ssl allows TLS 1.1 and cipher suites including TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA. CSPM reports LOW because TLS 1.1 is not completely deprecated and the policy has a minimum TLS version configured (unlike policies with no minimum). The V2C (Vehicle-to-Cloud) API endpoint serves authenticated vehicle command-and-control traffic. TLS 1.1 and CBC cipher suites are vulnerable to BEAST and Lucky13 attacks, putting vehicle command integrity at risk.
why_misclassified: EC-11: scanner scores based on presence of a minimum TLS version (any) rather than whether the minimum meets current standards. TLS 1.1 with CBC ciphers is considered broken for V2X security per UNECE WP.29 cybersecurity guidelines.
detection_signal: SSL policy hyundai-connected-car-ssl minimum TLS 1.1 — LOW: TLS version policy configured
ground_truth: UNECE WP.29 Annex 5 requires TLS 1.2+ with forward secrecy for V2C communications. TLS 1.1 with CBC is vulnerable to BEAST (CVE-2011-3389). Vehicle command channels must use TLS 1.2+ with ECDHE. Current policy violates WP.29 cybersecurity requirements.
remediation_impact: Update SSL policy minimum to TLS 1.2, restrict to ECDHE cipher suites. Validate that all vehicle firmware versions support TLS 1.2 (all models after 2019 do). Legacy 2018 Tucson (1.2% of fleet) may require separate policy.

scenario: Azure AD user svc-ota-deploy@hyundai.com has Owner role on subscription hyundai-connected-prod with no MFA enrollment. CSPM reports INFO because the account shows recent activity (login 3 days ago) and has a valid license. This service account owns the production subscription containing OTA update infrastructure for 1.2M Hyundai vehicles. No MFA means a compromised password could give an attacker full control over OTA update pipelines, enabling malicious firmware delivery.
why_misclassified: EC-48: scanner treats recent activity as a health indicator rather than flagging MFA absence on a privileged account. Account activity does not compensate for missing MFA on an Owner-role service principal.
detection_signal: Azure AD svc-ota-deploy@hyundai.com Owner role, active 3 days ago — INFO: account active and licensed
ground_truth: Owner role with no MFA on OTA infrastructure subscription is a CRITICAL finding. A compromised password enables full subscription control including modification of OTA pipelines, potentially enabling malicious firmware delivery to 1.2M vehicles. TISAX AL3 requires MFA for all privileged identities.
remediation_impact: Immediate: enable Conditional Access policy requiring MFA for all Owner-role accounts. Transition svc-ota-deploy to service principal with Managed Identity. Remove human-format credentials from OTA deployment pipeline.

scenario: GCP service account key for kia-adas-inference@kia-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com is 89 days old. CSPM reports LOW because the organization policy enforces 90-day key expiry and this key has not yet expired. The key is embedded in 340 ADAS inference edge devices deployed in Kia manufacturing plants. When the key expires tomorrow, all ADAS inference will fail simultaneously across all plants, halting production. There is no automated rotation mechanism.
why_misclassified: EC-14: scanner reports status as LOW because the key hasn't expired yet, missing the operational impact of imminent expiration across 340 production edge devices with no rotation automation.
detection_signal: Service account key kia-adas-inference age 89 days — LOW: key within 90-day rotation policy window
ground_truth: Key expires in 24 hours. 340 edge devices will lose ADAS inference capability simultaneously. No automated rotation pipeline exists. Manual rotation of 340 devices requires 48-72 hours minimum. Plants will be halted.
remediation_impact: Emergency: rotate key immediately, push to all 340 devices via MDM (if available) or manual intervention. Long-term: implement Workload Identity Federation for edge devices or certificate-based auth with auto-rotation.

scenario: IAM role hyundai-telematics-processor-role has an inline policy with Action: s3:* on a specific bucket ARN (arn:aws:s3:::hyundai-telematics-raw). CSPM rates this INFO because the resource scope is specific (not Resource: *). The role is used by the telemetry processing Lambda which should only need s3:GetObject and s3:PutObject. The s3:* wildcard includes s3:DeleteBucket, s3:PutBucketPolicy, and s3:PutBucketAcl — actions that could allow the Lambda to expose or delete the entire raw telemetry archive.
why_misclassified: EC-25: scanner evaluates resource scope (specific bucket ARN = good) without checking action scope. Action wildcard s3:* on a sensitive bucket grants destructive capabilities (DeleteBucket, PutBucketPolicy) to a processing Lambda.
detection_signal: IAM role hyundai-telematics-processor-role s3:* on specific resource — INFO: resource-scoped policy, not wildcard resource
ground_truth: s3:* on the raw telemetry bucket grants the Lambda ability to delete the bucket, modify its ACL, or change its bucket policy. A compromised Lambda could expose or destroy the entire raw telemetry archive. Minimum permissions are s3:GetObject and s3:PutObject.
remediation_impact: Replace inline policy Action: s3:* with explicit actions [s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject] on the telemetry bucket. Also grant s3:ListBucket on the bucket for prefix listing.

scenario: GKE cluster hyundai-connected-services-gke has Kubernetes Network Policy disabled. CSPM reports HIGH for missing pod-level network isolation. This cluster uses Google Cloud's Dataplane V2 (eBPF-based) which implements network policy enforcement natively without requiring the Kubernetes NetworkPolicy resource. The NetworkPolicy feature gate is disabled because Dataplane V2 handles all network policy enforcement at the eBPF layer.
why_misclassified: EC-10: GKE Dataplane V2 provides network policy enforcement via eBPF regardless of the Kubernetes NetworkPolicy feature gate. Scanner checks for the Kubernetes-native NetworkPolicy feature without detecting Dataplane V2 enforcement.
detection_signal: GKE cluster hyundai-connected-services-gke network policy disabled — HIGH: no pod-level network isolation in connected vehicle cluster
ground_truth: GKE Dataplane V2 (Cilium eBPF) enforces network policies at the kernel level. The Kubernetes NetworkPolicy feature gate being disabled does not indicate absence of enforcement when Dataplane V2 is the network plugin.
remediation_impact: Enabling Kubernetes NetworkPolicy feature gate on a Dataplane V2 cluster is a no-op — enforcement already happens at eBPF layer. No functional change but could be enabled for documentation/policy reasons.

scenario: RDS instance hyundai-vehicle-vin-db has DeletionProtection=false. CSPM reports HIGH for automotive production database without deletion protection. This RDS instance is covered by AWS Backup with daily snapshots retained for 35 days and weekly retained for 1 year. A Service Control Policy at the AWS Organization level (SCP-PROD-001) denies rds:DeleteDBInstance for all principals in production accounts except the dedicated DBA role, which requires MFA and PIM approval to assume.
why_misclassified: EC-53: deletion protection at RDS level is redundant when SCP-level deletion denial and backup policies provide equivalent or stronger protection. Scanner evaluates resource-level configuration without checking org-level SCP controls.
detection_signal: RDS hyundai-vehicle-vin-db DeletionProtection=false — HIGH: vehicle VIN database without deletion protection
ground_truth: SCP-PROD-001 denies rds:DeleteDBInstance for all production account principals except PIM-gated DBA role with MFA. AWS Backup provides 35-day daily and 1-year weekly snapshots. DeletionProtection=false is a cosmetic gap given SCP enforcement.
remediation_impact: Enabling DeletionProtection is a one-line Terraform change and is recommended as defense-in-depth. However, the CRITICAL/HIGH urgency is unwarranted given SCP and backup controls.

scenario: Azure VM kia-hmi-test-server-prod has NSG allowing RDP (TCP 3389) from 10.0.0.0/8. CSPM reports LOW because the source is a private RFC1918 range. The 10.0.0.0/8 range encompasses the entire HMG corporate network including Tier-1 supplier VPN pools, contractor networks, and development environments. The VM hosts HMI (Human-Machine Interface) software signing keys used to sign firmware deployed to Kia vehicle infotainment systems. Access from any of the ~50,000 corporate network users (including contractors) puts signing keys at risk.
why_misclassified: EC-16: scanner treats RFC1918 as a safe source without evaluating the breadth of 10.0.0.0/8 (entire corporate network including contractors) or the criticality of the protected asset (HMI signing keys).
detection_signal: VM kia-hmi-test-server-prod NSG allows RDP from 10.0.0.0/8 — LOW: private network RDP source
ground_truth: HMI signing keys on this server are used to sign vehicle infotainment firmware. RDP from 10.0.0.0/8 includes ~50K users including contractors. A compromised signing key could enable malicious HMI firmware deployment to all Kia vehicles with OTA capability.
remediation_impact: Restrict NSG to specific signing operator workstation IPs (3 machines). Move to Azure Bastion with PIM for all RDP access. Migrate signing keys to Azure Dedicated HSM.

scenario: Cloud Function hyundai-vehicle-command-dispatcher has HTTP trigger with allUsers invoker. CSPM reports HIGH for unauthenticated Cloud Function on vehicle command path. The Cloud Function is fronted by API Gateway with a JWT authorizer. allUsers is set at the Cloud Function level to allow API Gateway (which uses a Google-managed service account) to invoke it without needing per-request IAM auth tokens. The API Gateway validates the client JWT before routing to the Cloud Function.
why_misclassified: EC-34: allUsers at function level is required for API Gateway integration pattern. The authentication is enforced at the API Gateway layer. Scanner evaluates function-level IAM without checking API Gateway auth configuration.
detection_signal: Cloud Function hyundai-vehicle-command-dispatcher allUsers invoker — HIGH: vehicle command function unauthenticated
ground_truth: API Gateway validates JWT (Hyundai BlueLink app tokens) before routing. allUsers on the Cloud Function is required for the API Gateway service account to route traffic without IAM credentials on every request. This is the recommended GCP API Gateway + Cloud Functions architecture.
remediation_impact: Removing allUsers breaks API Gateway routing to the Cloud Function. Alternative: use Cloud Functions with Cloud Run (allows OIDC token injection). Migration is planned for Q2.

scenario: SNS topic hyundai-recall-broadcast does not use KMS encryption. CSPM reports MEDIUM for unencrypted SNS topic in automotive environment. The recall broadcast topic sends NHTSA-mandated recall notifications that are simultaneously published to the NHTSA public database. The notification content is public information by regulatory requirement (FMVSS 573). There is no sensitive data in recall broadcast messages.
why_misclassified: EC-26: KMS encryption evaluated as blanket requirement without considering that the data transmitted is public regulatory content by law. Encrypting recall notifications that are simultaneously published publicly provides no security benefit.
detection_signal: SNS topic hyundai-recall-broadcast no KMS encryption — MEDIUM: automotive recall notifications unencrypted in transit
ground_truth: NHTSA recall notifications are publicly mandated disclosures. SNS delivers over HTTPS (TLS in transit). At-rest encryption via KMS is not meaningful for data that is simultaneously published to NHTSA public registry.
remediation_impact: Adding KMS encryption to the recall broadcast topic is a valid hygiene change but provides no security benefit for public-by-law content.

scenario: Azure App Service hyundai-dealer-api has App Service Authentication (Easy Auth) disabled. CSPM reports HIGH for unauthenticated app service in automotive production. The dealer API uses a custom OAuth 2.0 implementation with Hyundai's internal dealer identity provider (not Microsoft identity). Easy Auth would force Microsoft identity, which is incompatible with the Hyundai dealer IdP. The app validates Hyundai dealer JWT tokens in application middleware (ASP.NET Core authentication middleware).
why_misclassified: EC-43: Easy Auth is Microsoft's hosted auth layer. Custom application-layer authentication is a legitimate alternative when the IdP is not Microsoft identity. Scanner equates Easy Auth disabled with 'no authentication.'
detection_signal: App Service hyundai-dealer-api Easy Auth disabled — HIGH: automotive dealer API without authentication
ground_truth: ASP.NET Core authentication middleware validates Hyundai dealer JWTs on every request. Easy Auth is not used because the Hyundai dealer IdP is not compatible with the Easy Auth configuration. Authentication is enforced at the application layer.
remediation_impact: Enabling Easy Auth would break dealer authentication entirely (Hyundai dealer IdP not supported by Easy Auth). Custom middleware auth is the required implementation for this IdP.

scenario: Cloud Memorystore Redis instance kia-session-cache does not have AUTH enabled. CSPM reports HIGH for unauthenticated Redis in automotive production. The Redis instance is configured with authorized_network restricted to the GKE private subnet (10.100.0.0/24). Only pods in the kia-session namespace with the network policy allowing egress to the Redis IP can reach the instance. VPC Service Controls perimeter prevents access from outside the project boundary.
why_misclassified: EC-08: Redis AUTH provides application-layer authentication. Network isolation (authorized_network + VPC Service Controls + K8s network policy) provides equivalent access restriction. Scanner requires AUTH without evaluating network controls.
detection_signal: Memorystore Redis kia-session-cache AUTH disabled — HIGH: vehicle session cache unauthenticated
ground_truth: Redis reachable only from 10.100.0.0/24 GKE private subnet. K8s NetworkPolicy restricts Redis access to kia-session namespace pods. VPC-SC perimeter prevents cross-project access. AUTH adds defense-in-depth but network controls make this informational.
remediation_impact: Enabling Redis AUTH requires application code changes to pass AUTH password on every connection. Should be added as defense-in-depth but urgency is LOW given network isolation.

scenario: AWS Backup vault hyundai-connected-backup-vault stores backups without a Vault Lock policy. CSPM reports INFO because the vault uses AWS-managed KMS key for encryption. However, the backup vault contains backups of DynamoDB tables storing vehicle authentication tokens, session data, and connected service credentials for 3.4M BlueLink users. Without Vault Lock, an administrator with BackupAdmin role could delete backups and cover traces of a ransomware or insider threat incident.
why_misclassified: EC-30: scanner checks for encryption (present) but not for Vault Lock immutability. Encrypted but deletable backups are inadequate for sensitive data recovery scenarios where insider threat or ransomware is the concern.
detection_signal: Backup vault hyundai-connected-backup-vault KMS encrypted — INFO: backup vault uses managed encryption
ground_truth: Backup vault stores authentication data for 3.4M users. Vault Lock in Compliance mode would prevent backup deletion even by administrators. Without Vault Lock, a compromised BackupAdmin credential could delete all recovery points, making ransomware recovery impossible.
remediation_impact: Enable Backup Vault Lock in Compliance mode with 14-day cool-off period. Vault Lock is irreversible after cool-off period — test in non-prod first. Provides immutable recovery points for ransomware defense.

scenario: Azure SQL Server hyundai-vin-lookup has Microsoft Defender for SQL disabled. CSPM reports HIGH for SQL without threat protection. The VIN lookup database is read-only with no direct internet connectivity — all queries come from the internal API layer. The SQL Server uses Azure Private Link, IP firewall restricted to API subnet (10.50.1.0/28), and Azure AD-only authentication. The threat surface (SQL injection, anomalous queries) is defended at the API layer with parameterized queries and application WAF.
why_misclassified: EC-47: Defender for SQL is valuable for internet-exposed or multi-tenant databases. This read-only, private-link-only database with API-layer query sanitization has minimal SQL injection surface. Defense at API layer is more appropriate than DB-level threat detection.
detection_signal: Azure SQL hyundai-vin-lookup Defender for SQL disabled — HIGH: VIN lookup database without threat protection
ground_truth: VIN lookup is read-only, Private Link only, Azure AD auth only. Parameterized queries enforced in API layer. WAF protects API surface. Defender for SQL would generate alerts for a threat surface that is effectively sealed by network and application controls.
remediation_impact: Enabling Defender for SQL adds $15/server/month. Would provide anomaly detection with high false positive rate for a read-only database with no SQL injection surface.

scenario: Cloud Run service hyundai-remote-diagnostics-api has CPU-always-on enabled. CSPM flags this as a compliance violation for cost efficiency policy. The remote diagnostics API must maintain persistent WebSocket connections to dealership diagnostic tools during active vehicle diagnostic sessions. Cold starts would drop active diagnostic connections, corrupting in-progress ECU calibration. CPU-always-on is required to maintain WebSocket connection state without cold start drops.
why_misclassified: EC-20: scanner flags CPU-always-on against a cost efficiency policy without evaluating the functional requirement (persistent WebSocket connections for ECU diagnostic sessions). This is a cost policy finding, not a security issue.
detection_signal: Cloud Run hyundai-remote-diagnostics-api CPU always-on — LOW: cost efficiency policy violation
ground_truth: WebSocket connections for vehicle ECU diagnostics require persistent CPU allocation. Cold starts drop active diagnostic sessions, potentially corrupting ECU calibration in progress. CPU-always-on is a functional requirement, not waste.
remediation_impact: Disabling CPU-always-on would drop all active diagnostic sessions during cold starts, corrupting ECU calibrations and requiring vehicle re-initialization. This is a patient safety analog in automotive context.

scenario: AWS root account for hyundai-telematics-prod has an active access key. CSPM reports CRITICAL for root access key. Security team investigation shows the 'root access key' flagged is actually an access key for an IAM user named root-monitor (not the actual AWS root account). The account has MFA enabled on the actual root account and no root access keys. The IAM user root-monitor was named following an old naming convention and is used for health monitoring.
why_misclassified: EC-39: scanner matches on IAM user name containing 'root' rather than specifically checking for the AWS account root (AccountID with no IAM path). IAM user root-monitor is not the AWS root account.
detection_signal: IAM user root-monitor active access key — CRITICAL: root account access key active in automotive production account
ground_truth: IAM user root-monitor is not the AWS root account. The actual AWS root account has no access keys and has MFA enabled. The naming is misleading but the security risk is to the IAM user root-monitor, not the root account.
remediation_impact: Rename IAM user root-monitor to monitoring-health-check to eliminate confusion. Rotate the access key per standard 90-day policy. No root account remediation needed.

scenario: Azure Key Vault kv-kia-telematics-legacy has soft delete disabled. CSPM reports HIGH for Key Vault without accidental deletion protection. Microsoft enforced soft delete on all Key Vaults in February 2025 — this vault was created before the enforcement and is shown as 'disabled' in the API response but soft delete is actually active (Microsoft enforced it retroactively). The API still returns softDeleteEnabled: false for vaults created before enforcement.
why_misclassified: EC-13: Azure API returns legacy softDeleteEnabled: false for vaults created before the February 2025 enforcement, but Microsoft retroactively applied soft delete protection. Scanner trusts API response without checking actual effective policy.
detection_signal: Key Vault kv-kia-telematics-legacy softDeleteEnabled=false — HIGH: automotive cryptographic keys without deletion protection
ground_truth: Microsoft enforced soft delete on all Key Vaults in February 2025. This vault's API field shows false due to creation before enforcement, but soft delete is active. Attempting to delete any secret fails with 'SoftDeleteEnabled' protection. This is an Azure API response inconsistency.
remediation_impact: No remediation needed for soft delete — it is already active. Update CSPM suppression list for this vault. File Azure Support ticket to get API response corrected.

scenario: GCP service account hyundai-ota-pipeline@hyundai-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com has roles/cloudbuild.builds.builder at project level. CSPM reports LOW because Cloud Build builder role is the standard role for build service accounts. However, this service account is used in the OTA firmware update pipeline. roles/cloudbuild.builds.builder grants the ability to trigger new builds, including builds that can run arbitrary code and push to Cloud Storage. A compromised OTA pipeline SA could trigger a build that packages malicious firmware.
why_misclassified: EC-02: standard role flagged as LOW because Cloud Build builder is a typical CI/CD permission. The scanner does not evaluate the criticality of what the builds can output (OTA firmware to millions of vehicles).
detection_signal: SA hyundai-ota-pipeline roles/cloudbuild.builds.builder — LOW: standard Cloud Build role
ground_truth: Cloud Build builder role grants ability to trigger builds that push to the OTA artifact bucket. A compromised SA could trigger a build with a modified Dockerfile, push malicious firmware, and trigger OTA distribution to Hyundai vehicles. Scope should be restricted to a custom role that allows only reading from the source repo, not triggering new builds.
remediation_impact: Create custom role with only cloudbuild.builds.list and cloudbuild.builds.get. Separate the OTA pipeline into a read SA (reads build artifacts) and a trigger SA (protected with additional approval gate).

scenario: DynamoDB table hyundai-ephemeral-sessions has Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) disabled. CSPM reports MEDIUM for production DynamoDB without backup. This table stores vehicle WebSocket session state for active connected vehicle sessions — each item has a 30-minute TTL. Sessions are ephemeral by design. If the table were corrupted, vehicles would simply re-establish sessions on reconnect. Historical session data has no value after expiry.
why_misclassified: EC-24: scanner applies PITR recommendation uniformly to all DynamoDB tables without distinguishing ephemeral session stores (where historical recovery has no value) from persistent data stores.
detection_signal: DynamoDB hyundai-ephemeral-sessions PITR disabled — MEDIUM: connected vehicle session data without backup
ground_truth: Table contains only active vehicle sessions with 30-minute TTL. All items auto-expire. Recovery of 30-minute-old session data would not restore any useful state — vehicles reconnect and create new sessions automatically.
remediation_impact: Enabling PITR adds $0.20/GB/month for a table where no historical data is useful. Vehicle sessions are stateless by design — reconnection is the recovery mechanism.

scenario: Azure Application Gateway hyundai-connected-appgw WAF is in Detection mode, not Prevention mode. CSPM reports MEDIUM for WAF not actively blocking in automotive environment. The WAF was placed in Detection mode 6 weeks ago during a V2C API update that introduced new header patterns that triggered WAF rules. The team is reviewing false positive WAF alerts before switching to Prevention mode. Detection logs show only 2 legitimate alerts in 6 weeks and 847 false positives from the new V2C header format.
why_misclassified: EC-47: WAF in Detection mode is a temporary operational state during tuning. Scanner flags the mode without context of the tuning process or the false positive volume that justified the mode.
detection_signal: App Gateway hyundai-connected-appgw WAF in Detection mode — MEDIUM: WAF not blocking in automotive production
