ground_truth: Detection mode is temporary (6-week tuning window). 847 false positives from new V2C API headers would cause production outages if Prevention mode were forced. Custom WAF exclusions being developed for the V2C header pattern. Prevention mode target: 2 weeks.
remediation_impact: Switching to Prevention mode now would block 847 legitimate V2C API requests per week, disrupting vehicle connectivity. Structured tuning with target Prevention mode date is the correct approach.

scenario: BigQuery dataset kia-vehicle-analytics-public is accessible to allAuthenticatedUsers. CSPM reports HIGH for public BigQuery dataset. This dataset was intentionally created as a public automotive analytics dataset containing aggregated, anonymized vehicle performance metrics shared with university research partners studying EV battery degradation. The dataset contains no PII, no individual vehicle identifiers, and all data is aggregated at the model/region level. Access requires a valid Google account, not truly public.
why_misclassified: EC-16: scanner flags allAuthenticatedUsers as equivalent to fully public without evaluating whether the data is actually sensitive or whether the sharing is intentional research collaboration.
detection_signal: BigQuery dataset kia-vehicle-analytics-public allAuthenticatedUsers access — HIGH: vehicle analytics data publicly accessible
ground_truth: Dataset contains only aggregated EV battery metrics (model, region, charge cycles) with k-anonymity applied (groups of 500+ vehicles). Intentionally shared with university research community. Contains no PII or vehicle identifiers by design.
remediation_impact: Restricting access to specific university Google accounts is good practice but the data itself is safe for public research use. Can be converted to specific domain allowlist if required.

scenario: Secrets Manager secret /hyundai/connected/mapbox-api-key has automatic rotation disabled. CSPM reports HIGH for non-rotating secret. The Mapbox API key is a third-party vendor key with an external rotation dependency — Mapbox does not provide a rotation API. Key rotation requires manual coordination with Mapbox (new key generation in Mapbox dashboard, update in Secrets Manager). Automatic rotation is architecturally impossible with Mapbox's current API.
why_misclassified: EC-55: scanner requires automatic rotation for all Secrets Manager secrets without evaluating whether the secret's source system supports programmatic rotation. Third-party API keys often cannot be automatically rotated.
detection_signal: Secrets Manager /hyundai/connected/mapbox-api-key rotation disabled — HIGH: mapping API key without automatic rotation
ground_truth: Mapbox API does not expose a key rotation endpoint. Automatic rotation is not technically possible. Manual rotation process documented in runbook with 90-day reminder. Last rotated 45 days ago.
remediation_impact: No technical solution available for automatic Mapbox key rotation. Consider migrating to a mapping provider with rotation API support (HERE Maps, Google Maps) in the next platform refresh.

scenario: Azure Storage account stKiaADASTrainingData has Shared Key authorization enabled. CSPM reports INFO because Shared Key is the default and the account has no public access. The storage account holds 2.7TB of raw ADAS training data including LiDAR point clouds of pedestrians, cyclists, and pedestrian behavior patterns at Kia's ADAS test facility. Storage access keys (which enable Shared Key auth) have full storage account access. If a storage access key were exposed, an attacker could exfiltrate all ADAS training data including personally-identifiable pedestrian behavior data.
why_misclassified: EC-22: Shared Key being the default causes it to be treated as an INFO baseline. The scanner doesn't evaluate the data sensitivity (TISAX-scoped ADAS training data with pedestrian PII components) or the breadth of access that storage access keys grant.
detection_signal: Storage account stKiaADASTrainingData Shared Key authorization enabled — INFO: standard storage configuration
ground_truth: Shared Key access grants full storage account control. 2.7TB of ADAS data includes pedestrian location and behavior patterns classified as PII under GDPR/TISAX. Disabling Shared Key and requiring Azure AD would prevent key compromise from enabling full data exfiltration.
remediation_impact: Disable Shared Key authorization (allowSharedKeyAccess=false), migrate all access to Azure AD with Storage Blob Data Reader/Contributor roles on specific containers. TISAX AL2 requires access control based on identity, not shared keys.

scenario: GCP backend service hyundai-internal-adas-api does not have Cloud Armor policy attached. CSPM reports HIGH for internal backend service without DDoS protection. This backend service is an internal load balancer (scheme=INTERNAL) serving traffic only within the GCP VPC — it has no external IP and is unreachable from the internet. Cloud Armor is only applicable to external HTTP(S) load balancers, not internal load balancers.
why_misclassified: EC-11: scanner applies Cloud Armor check to all backend services regardless of load balancer scheme. Cloud Armor is technically incompatible with internal load balancers — it can only be attached to external HTTP(S) load balancers.
detection_signal: Backend service hyundai-internal-adas-api no Cloud Armor policy — HIGH: ADAS API without DDoS protection
ground_truth: Internal load balancer scheme (INTERNAL) cannot have Cloud Armor attached. Cloud Armor is an external edge security product. Internal backend services are protected by VPC network policies, not Cloud Armor. Finding is technically impossible to remediate as stated.
remediation_impact: Cloud Armor cannot be attached to internal load balancers. This finding requires CSPM rule suppression for internal backend services.

scenario: AWS Config rule restricted-ssh reports EC2 instance hyundai-v2x-rsu as noncompliant (SSH allowed inbound). CSPM forwards this as HIGH compliance violation. The EC2 instance is the V2X roadside unit management interface that requires SSH access from the field engineering team to configure DSRC radio parameters. The SSH source is restricted to the field engineering VPN CIDR (172.16.50.0/28) in the security group rule. The Config rule restricted-ssh uses a blanket check for any inbound SSH without evaluating source restrictions.
why_misclassified: EC-30: Config rule restricted-ssh triggers on any security group with inbound TCP 22 regardless of source restriction. SSH from 172.16.50.0/28 (12 hosts) is meaningfully different from SSH from 0.0.0.0/0.
detection_signal: Config rule restricted-ssh noncompliant hyundai-v2x-rsu — HIGH: V2X roadside unit SSH noncompliant
ground_truth: SSH restricted to 172.16.50.0/28 (field engineering VPN, 12 hosts max). Config rule restricted-ssh is a coarse check for any inbound SSH. The specific CIDR restriction means this is a false trigger of the Config rule, not a policy violation.
remediation_impact: Deploy a custom Config rule that evaluates SSH source CIDRs (allowing specific /28 or /30 ranges while flagging /0 or /8 sources). Suppress this specific instance against the coarse restricted-ssh rule.

scenario: Azure Network Watcher is not enabled in australiasoutheast region for the Kia connected services subscription. CSPM reports MEDIUM for Network Watcher gap. Kia connected services operate exclusively in australiaeast and australiasoutheast regions. Network Watcher is enabled in australiaeast. The australiasoutheast region contains no VNets, no NICs, and no resources — it is an empty region in the subscription.
why_misclassified: EC-37: scanner enumerates all Azure regions and checks for Network Watcher in each, regardless of whether resources exist in that region. An empty region has no network traffic to monitor.
detection_signal: Network Watcher not enabled in australiasoutheast — MEDIUM: network monitoring gap in automotive subscription
ground_truth: No Azure resources exist in australiasoutheast for this subscription. Network Watcher monitors network traffic for VNets and NICs — none exist in this region. Enabling Network Watcher in an empty region generates no data and incurs minimal but unnecessary cost.
remediation_impact: Enabling Network Watcher in empty regions costs ~$1/month per region. Provides zero monitoring value without resources. CSPM rule should be configured to skip regions with no VNet resources.

scenario: GCS bucket hyundai-lidar-raw-temp has versioning disabled. CSPM reports MEDIUM for production bucket without versioning. This bucket is a pipeline staging bucket — LiDAR point clouds are uploaded, processed within 4 hours, and deleted. Objects in this bucket are transient processing artifacts with no long-term value. The bucket has a 24-hour lifecycle rule to delete objects. Versioning would retain deleted objects for 90 days, consuming massive storage for transient data with no recovery value.
why_misclassified: EC-18: versioning recommended for all production buckets without evaluating the transient nature of the data. Versioning of ephemeral pipeline staging data creates storage overhead with zero business value.
detection_signal: GCS bucket hyundai-lidar-raw-temp versioning disabled — MEDIUM: production bucket without data versioning protection
ground_truth: Pipeline staging bucket with 24-hour lifecycle deletion. Objects are transient LiDAR processing inputs — no recovery value after processing. Versioning would retain deleted objects and multiply storage costs by 10-15x for data that has no recovery use case.
remediation_impact: Enabling versioning on this staging bucket would retain 90 days of deleted LiDAR files, estimated 15TB additional storage at significant cost. No business case for recovering processed-and-deleted pipeline inputs.

scenario: AWS Inspector v2 is not enabled for EC2 and Lambda scanning in account hyundai-adas-prod. CSPM reports HIGH for missing vulnerability scanning. The account uses a third-party vulnerability management platform (Qualys) integrated via SSM. Qualys scans all EC2 instances with agent-based scanning (QCA), provides CVE correlation, and feeds the automotive security team's existing vulnerability workflow. Inspector would duplicate scanning and generate parallel alert queues.
why_misclassified: EC-44: scanner requires AWS-native Inspector without evaluating whether a third-party VM platform provides equivalent coverage. Qualys with SSM agent provides comprehensive vulnerability scanning compatible with ISO 21434 requirements.
detection_signal: AWS Inspector v2 not enabled — HIGH: automotive production account without vulnerability scanning
ground_truth: Qualys Cloud Agent on all EC2 instances provides continuous vulnerability scanning. Qualys is the enterprise vulnerability management platform feeding the automotive security program. Enabling Inspector would create duplicate findings requiring reconciliation.
remediation_impact: Enabling Inspector alongside Qualys creates duplicate scanning overhead and requires vulnerability management tooling updates to deduplicate findings. Qualys provides equivalent or superior coverage.

scenario: NSG hyundai-ota-subnet-nsg has outbound rule AllowInternetOutbound allowing all outbound traffic. CSPM reports INFO because outbound AllowInternet is the Azure default NSG rule. The subnet contains the OTA server that distributes firmware updates to 1.2M Hyundai vehicles. Unrestricted outbound access means the OTA server could be used as a pivot to exfiltrate data to arbitrary internet destinations if compromised, bypassing TISAX data loss controls.
why_misclassified: EC-41: Azure's default outbound rule is treated as expected baseline with INFO severity. For OTA infrastructure under UNECE WP.29 cyber security requirements, unrestricted outbound from OTA servers represents a significant exfiltration risk if compromised.
detection_signal: NSG hyundai-ota-subnet-nsg AllowInternetOutbound default rule — INFO: standard Azure outbound policy
ground_truth: OTA server subnet needs outbound only to: vehicle CDN endpoints (specific IPs), internal artifact storage, and OTA signing service. Unrestricted outbound allows a compromised OTA server to contact attacker infrastructure, exfiltrate firmware signing keys, or download additional payloads.
remediation_impact: Add deny-all-outbound rule and explicit allow rules for known OTA CDN IPs, artifact storage (Private Endpoint), and signing service. Implement Azure Firewall for OTA subnet egress inspection per UNECE WP.29 network segmentation requirements.

scenario: Compute Engine instance kia-canbus-gateway has serial port access enabled. CSPM reports MEDIUM for serial port enabled on production automotive VM. This instance runs the CAN bus gateway software for manufacturing line integration. Serial port access is required by the Hyundai production IT team to perform out-of-band diagnostics on CAN bus timing issues without network access. Serial port access in GCP requires valid GCP IAM authentication (gcloud compute connect-to-serial-port) — it is not an unauthenticated access vector.
why_misclassified: EC-26: serial port access in GCP requires IAM authentication via gcloud CLI. It is not a raw serial console — it is IAM-gated. Scanner flags serial port enabled as a risk without noting the IAM authentication requirement.
detection_signal: Compute instance kia-canbus-gateway serial port enabled — MEDIUM: production automotive VM serial console accessible
ground_truth: GCP serial port access requires gcloud compute connect-to-serial-port with valid IAM credentials and roles/compute.instanceAdmin. The serial port is not an unauthenticated back door. Used for emergency CAN bus diagnostics by authorized production IT staff.
remediation_impact: Disabling serial port removes the only out-of-band diagnostic path for CAN bus timing issues. Would require physical access to the manufacturing floor server rack for equivalent diagnostics.

scenario: Route 53 hosted zone hyundai-internal.corp does not have DNSSEC enabled. CSPM reports MEDIUM for DNS without validation. hyundai-internal.corp is a private hosted zone (associated with the internal VPC only, not resolvable from internet). DNSSEC is designed to protect against DNS spoofing on the public internet. Private hosted zones are only resolvable within the VPC and are not exposed to the public DNS namespace where DNSSEC attacks occur.
why_misclassified: EC-48: DNSSEC check applied uniformly to all hosted zones regardless of public/private classification. DNSSEC protects public-facing DNS. Private hosted zones accessible only within a VPC have no attack surface that DNSSEC addresses.
detection_signal: Route 53 hosted zone hyundai-internal.corp DNSSEC disabled — MEDIUM: automotive corporate DNS without validation
ground_truth: Private hosted zone only. DNS queries resolved within VPC only, not exposed to internet. DNSSEC protects against internet-based cache poisoning attacks. No such attack vector exists for a VPC-internal private zone.
remediation_impact: DNSSEC for Route 53 private zones has limited tooling support and Route 53 does not officially support DNSSEC for private hosted zones. This is an inapplicable recommendation.

scenario: Azure Function App kia-battery-telemetry-fn runs on .NET 6.0 which reached Microsoft end-of-life in November 2024. CSPM reports HIGH for deprecated runtime on battery telemetry function. The function processes HV battery thermal data from 890K Kia EVs. Runtime upgrade to .NET 8.0 is blocked by the Kia EV battery management ISV (Dukosi) which certifies the telemetry processing library only for .NET 6.0. The ISV certification for .NET 8.0 is in progress with estimated completion Q2 2025.
why_misclassified: EC-54: deprecated runtime is a real risk, but HIGH severity doesn't account for the ISV certification constraint that legitimately blocks upgrade. The risk is MEDIUM, not HIGH, given the active upgrade path and the non-internet-facing nature of the function.
detection_signal: Function App kia-battery-telemetry-fn .NET 6.0 deprecated — HIGH: EV battery telemetry on end-of-life runtime
ground_truth: .NET 6.0 EOL means no further security patches from Microsoft. ISV certification blocks upgrade until Q2 2025. Function is not internet-facing (triggered by Event Hub). Severity is MEDIUM — real risk with documented upgrade path, not negligence.
remediation_impact: Upgrade blocked by ISV certification. Interim mitigations: isolate Function App in dedicated App Service Plan, enable Defender for App Service enhanced monitoring, track ISV certification progress.

scenario: GCP project kia-adas-prod has clouddebugger.googleapis.com API enabled. CSPM reports MEDIUM for Cloud Debugger API enabled in automotive production (deprecated API, potential debugging exposure). Cloud Debugger was deprecated by Google and the API is no longer functional — Google disabled all Cloud Debugger backends in 2023. The API appears enabled in the project's API list as a legacy entry but the service is non-functional.
why_misclassified: EC-07: scanner checks API enablement list without verifying whether the API is still operational. Cloud Debugger APIs are enabled in many legacy projects but the backend was shut down by Google, making the API effectively inert.
detection_signal: Project kia-adas-prod clouddebugger API enabled — MEDIUM: debugging API enabled in automotive production
ground_truth: Cloud Debugger service was shut down by Google (May 2023). Enabling or disabling the API has no effect as the backend is defunct. No debugging access is possible through this API regardless of enablement state.
remediation_impact: Disabling the API is correct hygiene cleanup but the security finding is invalid — the backend doesn't exist. Run gcloud services disable clouddebugger.googleapis.com as housekeeping.

scenario: ElastiCache cluster hyundai-adas-feature-store has in-transit encryption disabled. CSPM reports HIGH for unencrypted cache on ADAS feature store. The ElastiCache cluster runs in a dedicated VPC subnet with security group allowing inbound TCP 6379 only from the ADAS inference EKS node security group. The cluster is within the same VPC as the EKS nodes, so traffic never leaves the AWS network fabric. Application data is feature vectors (floating point arrays) for ML inference — not PII or vehicle commands.
why_misclassified: EC-35: in-transit encryption recommended for all caches without evaluating VPC network containment and data sensitivity. Feature vectors for ML inference on a VPC-internal cluster have minimal exposure if intercepted within the same AWS network fabric.
detection_signal: ElastiCache hyundai-adas-feature-store in-transit encryption disabled — HIGH: ADAS feature store unencrypted
ground_truth: Cluster in dedicated VPC subnet, access restricted to ADAS EKS node security group. Traffic between EKS nodes and ElastiCache stays within AWS network. Feature vectors are ML intermediate data, not PII. Risk is LOW, not HIGH. Enable TLS for defense-in-depth.
remediation_impact: Enabling TLS requires ElastiCache cluster replacement (cannot enable TLS on existing cluster). Replacement requires ADAS inference service downtime and cache warm-up period of 2-4 hours.

scenario: Azure Conditional Access policy Require-MFA-Admin targets the 'Administrators' named location exclusion for break-glass accounts. CSPM reports INFO because the CA policy exists and is enabled. The policy excludes break-glass accounts from MFA requirement — standard practice. However, the break-glass account hyundai-emergency-admin@hyundai.com is also a member of the Global Administrator role (not just excluded from MFA). An attacker who obtains the break-glass credentials has Global Admin access with no MFA requirement, no TISAX AL3 access control, and unlimited subscription access.
why_misclassified: EC-50: scanner validates that the CA policy is enabled and structured correctly (break-glass exclusion is standard). It does not check whether break-glass accounts have excessive role assignments that compound the exclusion risk.
detection_signal: Conditional Access Require-MFA-Admin enabled with break-glass exclusion — INFO: standard CA policy configuration
ground_truth: Break-glass account has Global Administrator role. Exclusion from MFA + Global Admin = unlimited Azure access with only a password required. Break-glass should have limited, time-bound emergency permissions, not Global Admin. This creates a credential compromise scenario with catastrophic blast radius including OTA infrastructure.
remediation_impact: Remove Global Administrator from break-glass account. Use Privileged Identity Management with eligible Global Admin assignment (must activate with justification). Implement Conditional Access for break-glass with at least IP restriction to known NOC IPs.
